**What DID ship — the defect that produced this.** `/profile/edit` accepted any string, saved it, and said nothing; the profile then fell back to the monogram, **which is indistinguishable from never having set an avatar**, so nothing on screen told the collector their value was the problem. Now: `classifyAvatarUrl` names the case and says what to do (*"That is a link to the OpenSea PAGE for your item, not to the picture itself … right-click the artwork, Copy image address"*), and the live preview **reports a failed load** and swaps in the monogram so it still matches the public page.

⚠ **WARNS, NEVER BLOCKS.** A host can be down for a minute; refusing the save would strand a collector over a transient failure. What was missing was any signal at all.

⚠ **It also flags `http://`, and that is a REAL asymmetry rather than pedantry**: the profile page renders an http image fine, but `app/api/og/profile/[username]` gates its prefetch on `startsWith("https://")`, so an http avatar **silently vanishes from the social card** — the one place the avatar is seen by people not already on the site.

⚠ **A TEST OF MINE CAUGHT A DEFECT THAT WOULD HAVE ARGUED WITH THE USER.** The host patterns started as `(^|\.)nbatopshot\.com$`, which matches **`assets.nbatopshot.com`** — the CDN that serves the artwork. So the warning fired on a direct image link, i.e. it told the collector the exact thing it had just asked them to paste was wrong. Apex + `www.` only now.

⚠ **AND A MUTATION THEN SHOWED THAT FIX WAS MASKED.** Widening the pattern back stayed GREEN, because the fixtures ended in `.jpg`/`.png` and the image-extension short-circuit answered before the host rule was consulted. Closed with an **extensionless** CDN fixture (`assets.nbatopshot.com/resize/media/abc123` — the real shape), which is the only case where the apex-only pattern is load-bearing.

⚠ **One implementation gap found by a test I expected to pass:** the preview reported the failure but kept rendering the broken `<img>`, because `showImage` read the URL only. `loadFailed` now feeds the BRANCH — a preview showing a broken-image icon where visitors see a monogram is the drift that component exists to prevent.

**Verified.** `tsc` clean · primary **EXIT 0** (91.75/79.17/93.46/93.82) · component **EXIT 0** (90.82/82.34/89.49/93.79) · **7 mutations red** (marketplace detection, CDN-subdomain widening, http warning, mid-typing silence, onError reporting, monogram swap, reset-on-change) with the baseline re-confirmed after each.

**STILL OPEN:** tomwagmi's avatar. Needs the direct image URL pasted by someone who can reach OpenSea; the new warning now tells them exactly how to get it.

**Revert:** `git revert <sha>` — nothing to unwind.

### 2026-08-16 · SHIPPED (Claude Code, interactive) — buyback-wallet analytics: 99.7% of the acquisitions cannot be priced, so the board separates volume from spend instead of summing them

**What shipped.** `/analytics/buyback` + `/api/analytics/buyback` — what Top Shot's secondary-buyback wallets accumulate over week / month / year / all-tracked-time, with most-acquired moments, priced spend, and seller leaderboards by both dollars and transactions. New MV `topshot_buyback_daily`, `refresh_topshot_buyback_daily()`, `rpc_topshot_buyback_analytics(text,int)`, pg_cron jobid **333** (`51 8 * * *`), plus `lib/analytics/buyback.ts`, `components/analytics/BuybackDashboard.tsx`, a thin server `page.tsx`, an `/analytics` hub card, and 33 tests across three files.

⚠ **THE MEASUREMENT THAT DECIDED THE DESIGN — the headline metric the request asked for is mostly unknowable, and the naive board would have said $0.** Of **161,797** buyback acquisitions, only **431 (0.3%)** carry a price. The main wallet `0x4d2c9216f1dca098` (NBATopShotCommunity) is detected **entirely** by the daily holdings-snapshot diff, and 100% of its **161,366** rows have **NULL price AND NULL seller** with `sold_at` midnight-pinned to the DETECTION date. It has **3** priced sales in `sales_2026` all year, totalling $801. So `sum(price_usd)` next to the acquisition count publishes the buyback programme at **~$0.05 a moment**, and a seller leaderboard for that wallet is structurally impossible, not merely empty. The second wallet `0xe1f2a091f7bb5245` (TopShot_Buyback_2) is the only one that trades where our `sales_2026` trigger prices it: 431 rows, **$10,081.93**.

⚠ **So the split is carried end to end rather than the question being dropped or faked.** `priced_acquisitions` travels beside `spend_usd` at every level (totals, wallet, edition, day); `spend_known` is an explicit boolean so a consumer cannot infer "spent nothing" from a null it failed to interpret; the seller panels state they describe only priced purchases; and the coverage notice is **SUPPRESSED** when everything in a window is priced, because a permanent caveat is its own false claim. `walletSpendDisplay` returns an em-dash, never `$0.00` — mutation-proven (swapping it for `formatUsd(0)` reds two tests).

⚠ **"All time" is labelled ALL TRACKED TIME.** Snapshot history begins **2026-06-09**, but the wallet already held **52,118** moments on 2026-05-06 — so an unqualified "all-time" implies we are showing the programme's full history when we are showing ~10 weeks of it. `observation_start` is returned by the RPC and rendered.

⚠ **`0xb6f2481eba4df97b` is deliberately OUT of scope** — it is tagged `pack_inventory`, is a pack-distribution account rather than a buyback account, and **none** of its 43,675 rows resolve to an edition. Wallet scope is driven off the `seeded_wallets` **`secondary_buyback` tag**, never a hardcoded address list, so a third buyback wallet appears the day it is tagged.

**Performance.** A single `group by edition_id` on the base table was a **5,765 ms seq scan** (6,327 buffers) — far too slow for a live route on this instance, and a dashboard needs ~6 of them per period. The MV collapses the natural grain **205,472 → 19,602 rows** and the RPC computes every panel in one pass: **2,159 ms, 60,991 buffer HITS but only 394 disk reads**, so it barely touches the throttled disk. Refresh measured **144 ms / 22 disk reads**. Reconciled exactly against the base table: 205,472 acquisitions, 431 priced, $10,081.93 on both sides.

⚠ **A `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` was aborted by the 60 s MCP timeout and left an INVALID 18 MB index** (`idx_tib_buyer_soldat_cover`, `indisvalid=false`) — write overhead serving no reads. **Dropped**; the MV made it unnecessary. Worth knowing generally: when the MCP times out on a CONCURRENTLY build, check `pg_index.indisvalid` rather than assuming the statement rolled back.

**Security.** An MV can carry neither RLS nor `security_invoker`, so anon/authenticated are revoked EXPLICITLY (this DB's `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES` means `FROM PUBLIC` alone is not enough). Verified `has_table_privilege` anon/auth **false**, service_role true; the RPC likewise. `check_secdef_anon_exec_drift()` **0**, `check_public_security_invariants()` **0 rows**, `check_anon_write_surface()` **0 rows** after the change.

**Verified.** `tsc` clean; primary **12,726** tests / 1,259 files green at 91.75/79.20/93.47/93.82 (thresholds 91.3/78.6/93.1/93.4); component **1,788** green at 90.78/82.30/89.41/93.75 (thresholds 90.3/81.6/89.1/93.2); all four ratchets, brand-token, proxy and both driver-leak guards unchanged. Three mutations killed. ⚠ `/analytics/*` pages remain **sign-in gated** and `/api/analytics/*` public — the existing posture, deliberately not changed here, since exposure is Trevor's call.

**Revert path.** Code: `git revert <the feat(analytics) commit immediately after this ledger commit>`. DB, in this order:
```sql

DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS public.rpc_topshot_buyback_analytics(text, int);
DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS public.refresh_topshot_buyback_daily();
```

### 2026-08-16 · SHIPPED (Claude Code, interactive) — the new concierge smoke check was measuring ITS OWN SIBLING'S FIXTURE and reporting an outage that was not happening

**What shipped.** `app/api/smoke-test/route.ts` — the "concierge answers rather than degrading" check now excludes `is_smoke_test` rows. New guard `__tests__/smoke-concierge-degraded-share-excludes-smoke-rows.test.ts`.

**The defect.** That check (added earlier today) reads `support_conversations` over 6 h and fails when the DEGRADED share crosses 50%. Its own comment says it measures *"what share of REAL conversations got a degraded fallback rather than an answer."* **It had no `is_smoke_test` filter.** Meanwhile its sibling — `support-chat graceful-degradation (synthetic Anthropic 4xx)` — POSTs `x-rpc-test-error-mode: credit_balance` on EVERY smoke tick, deliberately, to prove the degradation path works, writing a `concierge_unavailable` row with `is_smoke_test = true`. **A good test doing its job, and manufactured evidence for the other one.**

**Measured live before changing anything:** of **905** conversations since 2026-08-02, **902 were smoke tests and 3 were real**, and **ALL 863 degraded rows were smoke rows — real degraded conversations: ZERO.** Broken out by day, real traffic was **0 on nine of the last ten days**, then 3 on 08-16 — **all three SUCCEEDED**. So the alarm (Sentry `JAVASCRIPT-NEXTJS-2E`, 27 users, *escalating*) reported a total concierge outage that was not happening. ⚠ And with one synthetic degraded row guaranteed per tick against ~0 real traffic, **it could never have gone green on its own** — a permanent false page, which is the fastest way to get every other check on the board ignored.

⚠ **A CORRECTION TO THE RECORD THAT MATTERS MORE THAN THE FIX.** CLAUDE.md records "~780 degraded conversations since 08-02" and "150 `concierge_unavailable` vs 3 `general` in 24 h" as **user impact**. Those are smoke-test rows. Real degraded conversations in that window: **0**. ⚠ This does **NOT** prove the concierge was healthy then — there was independent evidence of an Anthropic 403 `credit_balance`, and Trevor found it by using the product — but the user-impact NUMBER came from the wrong rows and should not be requoted.

⚠ **THE SHARPEST FORM OF THE GUARD-SCOPE CLASS YET: a monitor whose input set includes the output of another monitor.** Every prior instance in this file is a guard blind to something *outside* its derived scope; this one is a guard that can *see itself*. Worth checking for wherever a check reads a table that the test suite also writes.

**Consequence, stated honestly rather than smoothed over.** With smoke rows excluded, real traffic is ~0–3/day, so the check will normally report `low_sample: true` and **no verdict**. That is the honest outcome and is deliberately NOT "fixed" by lowering `MIN_SAMPLE` or by counting smoke rows — a verdict from one conversation, or from a fixture we generated ourselves, is worse than an explicit no-verdict. It starts earning its keep the moment real traffic exists, which is exactly when its answer matters.

**Verification.** Guard is a SOURCE check and **strips comments first** — load-bearing, not tidy: the fix's own comment names `is_smoke_test` several times, so a raw grep would pass on the prose alone with the filter deleted (this repo has shipped that bug ≥6 times). Mutation-proven: removing the filter while leaving every comment intact reds 2 of 4 cases; restored byte-identical and green. It also pins that the sibling still manufactures those rows, so the reasoning is re-derived rather than trusted if that ever changes. Smoke suites **31/31**, `tsc` clean.

**REVERT:** `git revert <sha>` — restores the unfiltered query and deletes the guard. No DB or prod-state change.

Verified safe to drop: **zero** DB dependents (`pg_depend`/`pg_rewrite`) and **zero** repo consumers — this view is operator-diagnostic, read by no route, cron or function.

### 2026-08-16 · SHIPPED (Claude Code, interactive) — anon could invoke a 45.8 s / 17 GB pack-EV function that nothing calls; anon+authenticated EXECUTE revoked

**Applied to prod** — `audit_20260816_revoke_anon_exec_on_zero_caller_pack_fns` (in `schema_migrations`; committed file byte-identical).

**The finding.** `compute_pack_ev_from_pool_tier_weighted` was **anon-executable** and costs, measured live on dist_id 4184 (largest TS pool, 3,097 rows):

```
Function Scan ... (actual time=45761.922..45761.923 rows=1 loops=1)
Buffers: shared hit=2260782 read=24987 dirtied=492 written=3
Execution Time: 45762.053 ms
```

**~46 s and ~17.4 GB of buffer traffic per call, and NOTHING IN THE PRODUCT CALLS IT.** Reachability is not theoretical — a `SET LOCAL ROLE anon` probe returned `{"ok":false,"reason":"pool_empty"}`, i.e. it **executed** rather than being denied. The anon key ships in the browser bundle and PostgREST exposes every public function at `/rest/v1/rpc/<name>`; `proxy.ts` is irrelevant (route-gating ≠ data-gating, the 2026-07-19 Panini/Candy lesson), and all four backing tables are anon-SELECTable so it really runs.

⚠ **Severity is AVAILABILITY, not confidentiality.** It is SECURITY INVOKER, so the caller's own RLS applies and it leaks nothing an anon visitor cannot already read. What it offers is **unauthenticated compute amplification**: ~46 s of a pooled connection and ~17 GB of buffers per request on a 2 GB IO-budgeted instance that was **already saturated when this was found** (39 active backends / 27 on IO waits; `fmv-recalc` killed at `maxDuration` on ~63–75% of invocations). A handful of concurrent calls is a full outage, from an unauthenticated client, for free.

⚠ **WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT — the guard-scope class, again.** `check_secdef_anon_exec_drift()` only considers SECURITY **DEFINER** functions. This one is SECURITY **INVOKER** (`prosecdef=false`), so that check is structurally blind to it however often it runs green. **There are 86 anon-executable INVOKER functions in `public`** — filed as its own item, deliberately not swept here.

**Scope discipline.** Only the two functions that are BOTH anon-executable AND zero-caller were touched, where a revoke cannot break anything. Zero-caller verified three ways each: `pg_proc.prosrc` across all of public (0), `cron.job.command` (0), repo grep across `app/ lib/ workers/ scripts/ supabase/functions/` excluding migration history (0). `score_external_pack_drop` is included for surface reduction only — it is cheap (`external_pack_drops` is 7 rows / 105 moments). ⚠ A prefix-grep trap: `get_pack_detail` looks called but every hit is the *different, live* `get_pack_detail_bundle`.

**Verified after apply.** `has_function_privilege` → anon **false**, authenticated **false**, service_role **true**, owner **true**. Functional probe: anon now raises `insufficient_privilege`. `check_public_security_invariants()` **0 rows**, `check_secdef_anon_exec_drift()` array length **0**, `check_anon_write_surface()` **0 rows** — posture undisturbed. Revoked BOTH halves in one statement (`FROM PUBLIC, anon, authenticated`) because this DB's `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES` grants explicit anon/authenticated rows a PUBLIC-only revoke leaves behind.

**REVERT:**
```sql
GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.compute_pack_ev_from_pool_tier_weighted(uuid, text, numeric, integer, jsonb) TO anon, authenticated;
GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.score_external_pack_drop(text, bigint) TO anon, authenticated;
```
(`git revert <sha>` restores the migration file but does **not** undo the grant — run the SQL above.)

### 2026-08-16 · SHIPPED (Claude Code, interactive) — `v_pack_pipeline_health` rebuilt: All Day arms added, two by-design-complete cursors stop crying wolf, and the view can actually be run

**What shipped (repo only — the migration is committed UNAPPLIED).** A pack-coverage audit across ownership / opens / purchases / sales for Top Shot + All Day found three defects in the one standing instrument over pack ingestion, and every gap the audit surfaced was invisible *because* of them:

1. **Top-Shot-only.** Four live All Day cursors (`allday_pack_purchases`, `allday_pack_purchases_backfill`, `allday_pack_opens_forward`, `allday_pack_opens_backfill`) appeared nowhere — All Day pack ingest could stop dead with the view still green.
2. **Cried wolf on two cursors that are complete by design.** `topshot_pack_purchases_backfill` + `topshot_pack_opens_backfill` stop at the worker's `TARGET_END_BLOCK` (151,610,000) and have not moved since 2026-05-21/22. The view rendered that as `seconds_since_update` — **2,098 h and growing forever**. An arm that can only get redder trains the operator to skim the whole view (the `ufc_fmv_stale_hours` cost).
3. **Its own cost made it unrunnable.** Two bare `count(*)` over `pack_purchases` (~302 k) + `pack_rips` (~3.66 M): `select * from v_pack_pipeline_health` **blew the 60 s budget outright** during the audit. Now planner estimates from `reltuples`, and recency rides `idx_pack_{purchases,rips}_collection_time`. The rebuilt body returns instantly.

**The load-bearing design decision is a REFUSAL.** `pack-events-ingest-backfill` drives FOUR cursors and writes ONE `pipeline_runs` row per invocation, so its `rows_found` belongs to no particular cursor — measured live, 7,155 found / 0 written in 24 h, *all* of it the All Day backfill re-treading blocks the forward cursor already covered. A view that split `rows_found` across its cursors would have marked both **finished** Top Shot cursors `wedged` — an incident manufactured out of the monitor's own blind spot. So `rows_attributable` is false for those four and the status is the neutral `static`: a description, not a verdict. Statuses: `missing_cursor | map_broken | not_running | live | wedged | quiescent | static`.

**A mutation forced a real design change.** Swapping `not_running` and `live` survived the whole file — they are independent in every state the fixture could produce. The contradictory state (cursor advancing while its pipeline logs zero runs) is *meaningful*: it means this view's own hardcoded cursor→pipeline map has drifted against a worker rename, which silently makes the wedged/quiescent verdict inert for every row sharing that name. Added `map_broken` ahead of both. ⚠ With it in place the swap is unobservable **again, correctly** — the two are now mutually exclusive — so that is documented in the test as redundant-behind-a-guard rather than papered over with a contrived fixture.

**Verification.** 9 mutations run: 8 killed (attributable-true, drop-attributable-guard, inner-join-event-cursor, drop-map_broken, map_broken-after-not_running, drop-an-All-Day-row, strip-security-invoker, quiescent→static, reltuples→count(\*)), 1 documented unreachable. Full DB suite **160/160 green** on a throwaway `postgres:16`; `migration-view-security-invoker-guard` + `db-invariants-drift-guard` **173 tests green**; `tsc` clean.

- **Nothing shipped. Read-only investigation; no DB write, no migration, no prod state change — so no revert path.** Filing: `docs/overnight/inbox/2026-08-16T1829Z-fmv-current-does-not-push-down-through-distinct-on.md`.

- ⚠ **THE FINDING: `fmv_current` is `SELECT DISTINCT ON (edition_id) … FROM fmv_snapshots` with NO WHERE CLAUSE, and `DISTINCT ON` is an optimization fence.** Measured on the same target editions — **literal `IN (a,b,c)` → 335 buffers / 83 ms** (becomes `Index Cond: edition_id = ANY(...)`), **`JOIN … ON edition_id` → 1,046,192 buffers / 28.7 s**, **`IN (SELECT …)` → 1,087,386 buffers / 34.9 s**. **~3,100× apart.** The two slow shapes materialize every one of ~26,000 editions' latest snapshot and then filter, to answer a question about 40. That is jobid 71's whole cost: 15 dists × ~28 s is past the 600 s budget before anything else competes.
- **Blast radius: 5 DB functions use the expensive JOIN shape** — `compute_pack_ev_per_edition_weighted` (confirmed by the timeout's own CONTEXT), `compute_pack_ev_from_pool`, `compute_pack_ev_from_pool_tier_weighted`, `backfill_pack_rip_metadata` (hourly `:53`), and **`sentinel_edition_coverage`**, a health check paying a full-table `DISTINCT ON` per run. The other 6 fns / 7 views / 1 matview / 19 repo files use other shapes and need individual checking — **do not assume all 38 consumers are affected.**
- ⚠ **`/api/fmv` IS FINE AND MUST NOT BE "FIXED".** It reads this view with 500-chunked supabase `.in()`, which PostgREST renders as a **literal** list — the 83 ms row. **The D27 fix that moved it onto `fmv_current` was correct**; this filing is not evidence against it.
- ⚠ **THREE HYPOTHESES I HELD AND MEASUREMENT KILLED, and the first is the one I would have shipped.** (1) *"Add `computed_at <= now()` for partition pruning"* — the documented `get_pack_detail_bundle` win does not apply: the empty 2025/2027 partitions cost **1 buffer each here**, so pruning saves ~2 of 1,046,192, **three orders of magnitude off the real problem.** (2) *"Jobid 71 is starved by a poison set"* — the insert filter and the `NOT EXISTS` recency gate really are asymmetric, so rejects should recur forever; measured **388 candidates, only 5 lack an ask.** Not the mechanism. (3) *"Stagger 71 away from jobid 217"* (`refresh_atlas_pack_ev`, 12 min later) — **0 overlapping pairs across 168 × 168 runs**; they never collide, consistent with the standing lesson that overlap tracks duration, not start minute.
- ⛔ **Do NOT `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW fmv_current`** when fixing this: it carries `reloptions = {security_invoker=true}`, and a `CREATE OR REPLACE` with no `WITH` clause **RESETS reloptions and silently strips it** — the footgun already paid for four times, invisible in the view's output. `ALTER VIEW`, or restate the `WITH`.
- **Why nothing shipped:** every implicated object is pack-EV / FMV / sentinel, all explicitly off-limits for autonomous change. The non-logic lever was considered and rejected on merit — **lowering `p_limit`** cuts runtime but reduces refresh coverage on a queue already 388 behind, and pack-EV publishes a public **+EV buy signal**, so making it staler is a product change wearing an optimization costume.

- ⚠ **An empty `pipeline_runs` window is CRITICAL, never ok — the load-bearing decision.** Retention is ~73 h, so the query returns nothing exactly once the outage outlives it: reading "no rows" as healthy would silence the arm **precisely when it finally mattered**. It falls back to the indefinite `pipeline_runs_daily` to DATE the outage, and when even that is unreadable it states the retention bound rather than inventing an age. Both branches are pinned.
- **Not shipped red, on purpose:** measured live at ship time it reads **warn (52.7 h)**, not critical. An arm that is red on arrival trains the operator to skim past it — the `ufc_fmv_stale_hours` cost. **It goes critical ~09:30Z on 08-17 if tonight's 13:30Z tick fails again, and back to ok if the retry works — so the arm and the fix validate each other on tonight's tick.** That is the one thing worth checking tomorrow.

By COUNT this route is a rounding error at 2; by RATE it is the worst on the board at **2 of 3 runs**. ⚠ **Count and rate rank these in opposite orders.** The durable rule: **the value of a retry scales inversely with cadence** — a `*/20` pipeline self-heals on its next tick, a daily batch has no natural retry — which is why the other ~49 were deliberately NOT swept (in most, the RPC *is* the work, so a retry re-runs expensive, not-always-idempotent work).

**What shipped:** `app/api/cron/ownership-onchain-walk/route.ts` + `__tests__/api-cron-ownership-onchain-walk-deep.test.ts` (+2 tests) + the corrected inbox filing. No DB, migration, cron, auth/`proxy.ts`, hot-wallet or FMV/pricing change.

The route holds a **720 s** budget and never touched it: it burned a whole day's tick without doing anything, twice. `topshot_ownership` froze at an 08-14 `observed_at` (267,742 rows — last-good, not empty; consumer `lib/set-completers-board.ts`).
- **The fix:** route the gating read through `rpcWithRetry` at **3 attempts / 20 s base / 300 s total**. ⚠ **The helper ALREADY classified this transient** (`rpc-with-retry.ts:281`, "connection pool") — the route was simply using a bare `supabaseAdmin.rpc()`. ⚠ **The batch-sized backoff is the load-bearing part, not the retry**: the helper's default is 3 attempts / **~250 ms**, and its own comment at line 265 records that lengthening it is "a product call" because it trades a 500 for a ~20 s hang. **That objection does not apply to a daily cron with nobody waiting** — which is exactly why the default was wrong here and right there. Sized to leave ≥7 min of walk budget; a slow-but-succeeding fetch degrades to PARTIAL progress (the queue is oldest-first and resumable), not an overrun.
- ⚠ **Shipped as a MITIGATION and labelled one in code, tests and the filing — it is NOT proven to fix it.** If the pool is saturated longer than 300 s the run still fails. It converts a guaranteed total loss into a likely recovery. **Judge it by `wallets_walked` on the next few ticks, not by the comment.**
- ⚠ **I CORRECTED MY OWN FILING FROM EARLIER THIS SESSION, AND BOTH OPTIONS I OFFERED WERE WRONG.** I flagged the 08-13 → 08-14 collapse (75,757 → 1,748 rows) as "queue draining **or** already degrading". It is neither: **`wallets_walked` is 799 on BOTH days** — the batch is a fixed wallet COUNT, so `rows_found` only tracks how many moments that batch happened to hold (whales one day, small wallets the next). **Expected variance, not a signal. Read `wallets_walked`, never `rows_found`, as this pipeline's throughput.** Offering two hypotheses and flagging them as needing one query is what made the catch cheap; publishing either as a finding would have been a fabricated regression.
- ⚠ **Pre-empted the obvious wrong fix, with a measurement.** `get_stale_ownership_wallets` is a **Parallel Seq Scan over all 267,742 rows / 4,230 buffers / `shared hit=3` (fully cold) / 2,390 ms** whose `LIMIT` sits above a HashAggregate that must consume every row — so **lowering `WALLETS_PER_RUN` buys identical scan cost and less work done**, the same scan-bound shape already recorded for `remap_topshot_realign_miskeyed_subeditions`. And 2.4 s ≠ 72 s: the failure is **pool-acquire, before execution**, so no index addresses it (the tempting `(owner_address, observed_at)` index-only scan is probably the measured-and-rejected `fmv_snapshots` heap-fetch trap, since this walk upserts the very table it reads).
- **Saturation-class, so deliberately NOT a separate investigation** per CLAUDE.md — same root cause as the entity-page aborts and the `fmv-recalc` kills. What is separate is the **silence**: no `pipeline_cadence_watchlist` entry, and ⚠ **a cadence entry would not help** — the cron fires perfectly and a failing run still writes a row, so recency reads healthy. The honest instrument is an OUTCOME check on `max(observed_at)` age; **left for a decision** (new alerting arm, and this repo has paid for `ufc_fmv_stale_hours` crying wolf).
- **Tests pinned in BOTH directions and mutation-proven.** Transient → retried and the run RECOVERS (`wallets_walked` 1, `ok` true); non-transient → **still fails fast at exactly one call**, because retrying eagerly would stall a cron for five minutes on a genuine logic error. Mutations: bare `.rpc()` → RED, `attempts: 1` → RED, `attempts: 9` → **survives**, correctly — the non-transient path breaks at the transience check before the count matters, so it is category-2 redundant-behind-another-guard and is documented rather than contrived around. Fake timers drive the 20 s backoff, so the suite stays at 462 ms.

### 2026-08-16 · SHIPPED (Claude Code, interactive, cont. — "keep going") — a concierge tool told collectors "this is not an error" about a feed that had written ZERO rows that day, and a test was pinning the reassurance

**What shipped.** `app/api/support-chat/route.ts` (`search_serial_deals`, all four exits + tool description + system prompt) + `__tests__/api-support-chat-tools-populated-4.test.ts`. No DB, migration, cron, auth, hot-wallet or FMV-math change.

**How it was found — by finishing the alert thread rather than declaring it done.** Having made a price-only alert able to fire, I checked whether the LAST leg delivers. `alert_deliveries`: **834 all-time, newest 2026-06-25 — 52 days ago**, while `alerts-dispatch`/`alerts-send` keep running. That turned out to be an **honest** silence (2 active subs: Trevor's, matching 0 at a true $4.00 floor, and a Blazers-rookie-special-serial sub against a 3-row pool) — but tracing *why* the pool is 3 rows found the real defect one layer down.

⚠ **THE FIND: the tool hard-coded a claim it cannot observe.** `search_serial_deals`' empty-state said *"The residential serial-listing feed refreshes every few hours; **this is not an error**"*, and the prompt told the model *"do NOT imply the feed is broken"*. Measured live: `topshot-active-listings-ingest` fails **`egress_blocked`** most sweeps (the Atlas WAF blocks the GHA runner IP; `workers/atlas-proxy` is the known fix and is still INERT), and on **2026-08-12 it wrote ZERO rows across all 5 runs of the day**. On a day like that the concierge told a collector nothing was listed below FMV **and explicitly reassured them nothing was wrong** — the failure-renders-as-data class with the reassurance written in as an instruction. **A tool cannot see its own health; it can only report how old its data is.**

⚠ **"Every few hours" was ALSO wrong, and measuring it is what stopped me picking a cry-wolf threshold.** Over the ~73 h `pipeline_runs` window there were only **5 successful sweeps** — gaps **min 3 h / median 6 h / p90 22 h / max 26.7 h**. A 24 h ceiling would fire during normal operation, which is the `ufc_fmv_stale_hours` cost this repo already paid. So the **AGE is the primary output** (stated on every response, and the model is required to state it), and `feed_stale` sits conservatively at **36 h**, clear of the worst observed normal gap — with the 5-sweep sample size recorded in place, because it cannot support a sharp threshold.

⚠ **ALL FOUR EXITS carry it, not just the one that was wrong.** The two empty exits claim the market is quiet; the two POPULATED exits can send a collector to a listing that has already sold, which is the same snapshot problem pointing at money. Sweeping the read rather than the site that failed.

⚠ **A TEST WAS PINNING THE REASSURANCE — second instance of this class today, and subtler than the first.** `expect(String(r.message)).toMatch(/not an error/i)`. The morning's instance pinned a *limitation*; this one pins a *reassurance*. Both are claims the tool could not support. Inverted to assert the phrase is **ABSENT** and the age fields are present.

⚠ **One mutation SURVIVED and it corrected my own comment.** Dropping `!freshErr` from the freshness read changes nothing — a failed `.maybeSingle()` nulls the row too, so both shapes fall through the same branch. **The load-bearing part is that an unresolved age stays `null` and is never defaulted to 0.** Same correction the `?? 0` sweep already made once; the comment now says so instead of claiming the error-check is the mechanism.

### 2026-08-16 · SHIPPED (Claude Code, interactive — Trevor: "if all I mention is a price, don't assume extra factors like FMV") — a silently-added filter made an alert narrower than the sentence confirming it, and nothing watched the concierge fail for 14 days

⚠ **ITEM 2 — THE DEFAULT THAT INVENTED A CRITERION.** "Alert me any time a Damian Lillard Archive moment lists for $0.60 or less" was SAVED as `max_price 0.60` **AND `min_discount 25`** — the tool's unconditional default. The confirmation said *"whenever a Damian Lillard Archive moment lists at $0.60 or under"*, so **the alert was strictly narrower than the sentence describing it**, and a $0.55 listing only 10% under FMV would never have fired. **Its silence is indistinguishable from "nothing has listed"** — the failure-renders-as-absence class applied to a promise. The default now applies **only when no `max_price` was given** (it still earns its place on an open-ended "good Blazers deals", where a threshold is the only thing between an alert and a firehose).

⚠ **MY FIRST FIX WOULD HAVE BEEN WORSE THAN THE BUG, AND THE DB CAUGHT IT.** I wrote `min_discount = null`. The column is **NOT NULL DEFAULT 25**, so every price-only alert would have thrown `23502` and created nothing at all. Found by running the UPDATE on the live row BEFORE shipping the code — the write failed, not the reasoning. **Ship-order luck; the durable rule is to exercise a schema assumption against the schema.**

⚠ **AND 0 IS NOT "NO FMV CONDITION" — THE SCANNER CANNOT EXPRESS THAT, so it is DISCLOSED rather than quietly re-hidden.** `build_deal_alerts_for_subscription` (and the dispatcher it mirrors) reads `cross_collection_deals_board` with `discount_pct >= COALESCE(min_discount, 25) AND fmv_usd > 0`. So even at 0 a listing **above** FMV, or on an edition with no FMV, still cannot fire. Trevor's ask is therefore **not fully deliverable by a tool change** — a true price-only alert needs a scanner change. Rather than claim it was done, `applied_filters` now states the residual condition in the user's own confirmation. **Open, filed, not done.**

**ITEM 1 — the confirmation now describes the SAVED ROW, filter by filter.** The tool returned only `{id, label, channels}`, so the model wrote the confirmation from the user's REQUEST and any added filter was invisible. It now returns `applied_filters` plus a note requiring every entry to be stated. The auto-label was fixed the same way — a row labelled "25%+ under FMV" that carries no discount filter is the same lie in the list view.

**ITEM 3 — the concierge can be DOWN FOR TWO WEEKS AND THE SMOKE TEST REPORTS `ALL PASSED`.** Measured: **150 `concierge_unavailable` vs 3 `general`** in 24 h, and ~780 degraded conversations from 2026-08-02 → 08-16 (Anthropic returning `403 credit_balance`). New HARD check `db:support_conversations.category` measures the **outcome** — the share of real conversations that got a fallback instead of an answer — for one indexed read and zero credits. ⚠ Keyed on **`category`, not the fallback COPY**, which is user-facing prose that will be reworded, taking a string-matching check quietly vacuous while still reporting green. ⚠ Carries a **5-conversation sample floor**: without it one failure on a quiet night reads as "100% degraded" and pages for nothing — this repo has already paid for a cry-wolf arm (`ufc_fmv_stale_hours`). Below the floor it PASSES with an explicit low-sample note rather than a verdict it did not earn. Smoke totals 54→**55**, hard 42→**43**.

**DB change (prod data, 1 row):** `alert_subscriptions fd0d7a2c-… min_discount 25 → 0`, widening Trevor's live Lillard alert. **Undo:** `UPDATE alert_subscriptions SET min_discount = 25 WHERE id = 'fd0d7a2c-3a31-4d94-9c91-0db7af2f697d';`

**Why this one.** Chosen by DERIVATION density rather than size — it carried **10** filter/sort/slice sites, three times the next page. It is the honesty board about **our own pack-EV model** ("the model says $X, packs actually pull $Y"), so every threshold decides which distributions a collector is shown as evidence the model is wrong — and all of it sat in a `page.tsx` that neither coverage gate measures.

⚠ **THE THREE BUCKETS ARE NOT SYMMETRIC, AND NOTHING SAID SO.** Reading the asymmetries as oversights is the mistake this module now prevents:
- **The fossil guard (`modeled EV <= 1.5 × price`) applies to `over` ONLY.** A depleted pool models at 40–86× its price and *by construction* looks like a massive over-valuation — so without it the "model over-values" board would be nothing but drained pools and the real over-valuations would be pushed off. On `under` a fossil is not a plausible member at all, so guarding there would exclude nothing while implying the lists are filtered alike.
- **`over` requires a modeled EV of $2, `under` only $0.50.** A ratio is a ratio: on a pack modeled at $0.30 a realized $0.10 reads as a dramatic over-valuation while being twenty cents. `over` is the accusatory list, so it carries the higher bar.
- **`onModel` ranks by SAMPLE SIZE, not ratio** — a band has no "most" end to sort toward, so the most-opened distributions lead as the strongest evidence.
- **The gaps between bands (0.6–0.8, 1.25–1.8) belong to nothing, deliberately** — a row in between supports neither claim, and widening a band to close a gap would put ambiguous evidence under a confident heading.

⚠ **TWO MUTATIONS SURVIVED AND BOTH WERE MY FIXTURES AGREEING WITH THEMSELVES.** Sorting `onModel` by ratio instead of opens passed, because I had given the most-opened row the *higher* ratio — both criteria produced the same list. And building `onModel` from raw rows instead of the priced set passed, because every unpriced fixture had a ratio *outside* every band. **A fixture only tests a discriminator when the two candidate implementations DISAGREE on it** — the third time this session that a survivor was a fixture problem rather than a missing assertion, and the shape is always the same.

**Also pinned:** the SQL gates the JS filter repeats. The price/model filters exist in BOTH places — the SQL copy is a cost optimisation (this view aggregates 2.8M rows; filtering cut 1,559 rows to 302, one page instead of two) and the JS copy is the correctness one, so the ranking cannot depend on the SQL having been written right. Dropping either is a real change, so both are asserted.

**Verified.** 14 mutations red: fossil guard dropped · fossil guard wrongly extended to `under` · fossil bound made strict · `over`'s EV floor lowered to `under`'s · each of the three bands' inclusivity flipped · `onModel` sorted by ratio · slice-before-sort · priced filter dropped · `low_confidence_ev` gate inverted · `n_opens` gate dropped · failed read reporting ok:true · `onModel` built from raw rows. ### 2026-08-15 · SHIPPED (Claude Code, interactive, cont. — "keep going") — closed the last named worker blind spot, and BOTH halves of it were parked behind a tooling gap that did not exist

**What shipped.** 3 worker tests (`pack-events-ingest`, 29 → 32 cases) + one additive helper field + the worker ratchet re-seated. Test-only; **no worker source change**, no DB, cron, auth or prod change.

⚠ **THE FINDING IS THAT THE PREMISE WAS WRONG, TWICE.** `vitest.workers.config.ts` had listed two items as unreachable "with a fixture alone". Both were reachable:
- The soft-budget bail-outs were said to need a fake clock. They do not — **driving `Date.now` from the FETCH STUB** (each event fetch advances a mutable value) is deterministic and never touches `vi.useFakeTimers`, so it cannot fight the `AbortSignal.timeout` shim the suite already patches. (Done earlier this session.)
- The chunked-write paths were said to need "a stub that fails the Nth chunk". **The sequence-aware fixture already does that** — an array payload yields one entry per `await`, so chunk N takes payload N. The only helper change needed was capturing the upsert **OPTIONS**, because `{ onConflict, ignoreDuplicates }` is what makes the replay safe and nothing in the suite could see it.
**Both were parked behind an assumed tooling gap that a few minutes of reading disproved.** The config comment now says so, because "recorded as unreachable" is exactly the note nobody re-checks.

⚠ **WHAT THE TESTS PIN: this worker runs TWO DELIBERATE CHUNK POLICIES, and the difference is the point.**
- **A failed WRITE throws and BLOCKS THE CURSOR.** With 401 rows chunked 400 + 1 and the second chunk erroring, the first 400 are durably banked *and* `writeCursor` is never reached — so the next tick replays the whole window. That is the fix for the recorded incident where a single 1796-row upsert timed out deterministically and **permanently wedged the cursor while the cron showed green**. Advancing here would step past 401 events of which 400 landed: one silently lost purchase, forever.
- **The replay that non-advance implies is safe ONLY because of `ignoreDuplicates` on the right conflict target** — asserted from the newly-captured options, since rows alone cannot show it. A plain insert, or `onConflict: "tx_hash"` alone, would double-count every row of the chunk that DID land.
- **A failed LOOKUP is collected and the cursor advances anyway.** 101 rips, id-lookup chunked 100 + 1, second chunk errors: the 100 that resolved are still linked, because aborting would throw away real work.

⚠ **AND THE COST OF THAT SECOND POLICY IS NOW PINNED AS A KNOWN PROPERTY.** The 101st rip's moment is skipped (*"skip rather than corrupt FK"*) and, because the cursor advanced past it, **it is never retried** — one moment permanently unattributed to its pack, and every pack-EV / pull-value surface loses that join. ⚠ **A second assertion of mine failed and the code was right again**: the run reports **`ok: false`** (it is `errors.length === 0`) *while the cursor advances*. So the operator gets a red run whose underlying work is not recoverable by acting on the red. **Reporting and recovering are separate things here** — stated plainly rather than left to be discovered during an incident.

**Ratchet re-seated in the SAME pass that measured the drift** — 84.4/71.2/83.2/87.5 → **85.1/72.1/83.8/88.1** against actuals 85.59/72.61/84.25/88.53, back to the ~0.4pt band. "Keep the buffer" is how the component gate reached ~13 points.

**Verified.** 9 mutations, each red: chunking removed · cursor advancing despite the throw · `ignoreDuplicates` dropped · wrong conflict target · write error swallowed · lookup failure made fatal · lookup errors swallowed · unresolved rip given a NULL FK instead of a skip · lookup chunking removed. Full primary suite **12,380 passed / 1,236 files**; worker gate **376 passed**; `tsc` clean.

**Revert:** `git revert <sha>` — test + config only, nothing to unwind.

What IS readable at runtime is the function's own source: `pg_get_functiondef` inside the test. **When a property is invisible in behaviour, the catalog is still a witness.**

**The five substantial ones, each pinned on its sharpest property:**

A partial sum is a SMALLER number that reads exactly like a real one — a 5-moment rip with 2 priced pulls would publish those 2 as the pack's worth, making a good pull look like a bad pack, failing in the reassuring direction so nothing reports it.

Two separate lookups, even two correct ones, would let a row carry one snapshot's price under another's confidence — **a STALE price wearing a HIGH label is a number a collector has no way to distrust**, on the portfolio store ~34 functions sum.

(2) My fetch-count assertion failed at **360** because the *other* backfill cursors were still walking and drowning the signal; parking them isolates the leg.

Fixed by putting a **SIBLING pack in the same batch**: a clean skip leaves it ripped, a crash loses it too. **When you assert that something is skipped, include something that must survive the skip** — otherwise "skipped" and "exploded" are the same assertion.

Replacing it with a plain assignment changes **nothing observable** and the pin stays green. Belt-and-braces is fine to keep; **describing it as a second enforced invariant is not**, because a future reader would trust a protection no test can detect the loss of. ### 2026-08-15 · SHIPPED (Claude Code, interactive — "concierge should pull cheapest listing / special-serial links" + "the discord bot didn't respond") — the concierge could not answer "is this one listed?" for ANY edition, and `/api/edition-floor` was answering with another edition's price

**Trigger.** A real Telegram reply: *"The live sniper feed doesn't filter by set name directly … it's not showing a current listing in the live feed — meaning nothing may be listed right now, or it's priced above the feed's current snapshot."* That is our indexing narrated back at a collector instead of an answer, and every clause of it turned out to be covering a different real defect.

⚠ **ROOT CAUSE 1 — every "listings" tool the concierge had was a DEAL board.** `search_live_deals`, `search_catalog_deals` and `search_serial_deals` all require a discount below FMV (`.gt("discount", 0)`), so an edition listed **at or above FMV returns nothing from all three** — and the bot read that emptiness as a fact about the market. **There was no tool that could answer "what is the cheapest one listed right now" for a named edition.**

⚠ **ROOT CAUSE 2 — `/api/edition-floor`, the one route that could have answered, was broken in three independent ways, and each failed SILENTLY.** (a) It posted `public-api.nbatopshot.com` **directly, with no `TS_PROXY_URL` and no `X-Proxy-Secret`** — Cloudflare blocks Vercel egress to that host, so in production the Top Shot leg hit its catch on **every call**. (b) `fetchFlowtyFloor(setID, playID)` **used neither argument**: it asked the collection-wide endpoint for the 48 cheapest TopShot listings on Flowty and returned the minimum **as this edition's floor**, which `selectCrossMarketFloor` then published as `crossMarketSource: "flowty"` — the sniper depth panel has been rendering another edition's price as "Cross-market $X on Flowty". (c) Every failure exit returned the same `{ floor: null, count: 0 }` as a genuinely unlisted edition, so **a blocked proxy, a GQL error and an empty order book were byte-identical to every caller** — the failure-renders-as-data class, and the direct cause of the sentence above.

⚠ **The data-source survey that shaped the fix (measured live, so nobody re-derives it):** `ts_listings` is **DEAD** — 1 row, last ingest 2026-05-15, ~3 months stale — so sniper-feed's Supabase listing path is inert. `cached_listings` holds **301 rows, 100% Flowty**, no `edition_id` column at all. `topshot_active_listings` is **258 rows / 231 editions** — the residential *chase-serial* feed, not an order book. **The only live per-edition ask source on the platform is the Top Shot GQL, through the proxy.**

**What shipped.**
- **`/api/edition-floor` correctness.** Routed through `TS_PROXY_URL` + `X-Proxy-Secret` (the pattern every sibling TS GQL caller already used); the unattributable Flowty leg is **removed, not repaired** — a wrong floor is worse than no floor, and that endpoint has no per-edition filter (`selectCrossMarketFloor` stays wired so an attributable venue is a one-line restore). Added a transport-level `ok`, and the route now **503s** when the marketplace was not reached instead of serving a 200 that reads as "nothing listed".
- **New concierge tool `get_edition_listings`** (32 → 33 tools) — per-edition floor, listing count, FMV + confidence, discount, edition URL, and any **#1 / perfect-mint serial currently listed with its own buy_url**. Ambiguous names return **candidates** rather than silently picking a row (attaching a real floor to the wrong moment is worse than asking). Backed by `lib/concierge/edition-listings.ts` so the logic sits in the measured gate.
- **`setName` filter on `search_live_deals`** — literally the thing the bot said it could not do.
- **System-prompt rule** making the three-way answer mandatory: `listed` / `none_listed` / **`unavailable`**, with an explicit ban on reporting `unavailable` as "nothing is listed" or substituting FMV for an ask, plus "never narrate our indexing to the user".

⚠ **THE HONESTY INVARIANT, since it is what a future refactor will destroy:** `listings_status` is derived from the **transport flag**, never from the row count. Deriving it from the count re-creates the original bug exactly. Mutation-proven in both files.

⚠ **DISCORD — the bot is not broken, and no code change can make a plain DM work.** Its endpoint is an **Interactions webhook**: it receives `PING` and `APPLICATION_COMMAND` and nothing else. Ordinary DM messages are **Gateway** events (`MESSAGE_CREATE`, behind the privileged `MESSAGE_CONTENT` intent) delivered over a persistent websocket that serverless cannot hold — so **a plain Discord DM produces no request to this app at all**. Telegram's webhook *does* take plain text, which is why the two behave differently. `/ask` is the only concierge path on Discord. Shipped: the alert DM now tells the user that (it is the message they are most likely to reply to), and **`GET /api/bots/discord/register`** reports what Discord actually has registered — `registered` / `missing` / `dm_capable`, never the token. ⚠ **Operator action may still be needed:** if `missing` contains `ask`, the one-time `POST` to that route has not been run since `/ask` was added, and the command will not appear in anyone's client — which is indistinguishable from a dead bot.

**Verified.** `tsc` clean; primary suite **12,218 passed / 1,232 files / 0 failures**; primary coverage **91.72 / 79.08 / 93.4 / 93.81** against the 91.3 / 78.6 / 93.1 / 93.4 ratchet. ⚠ **Three pre-existing assertions in `api-edition-floor-integration.test.ts` PINNED THE DEFECT and were repointed, with the reasoning kept in the file** — two asserted the global-Flowty floor as the edition's floor (green *because* they reproduced the bug), and one was titled *"reports null floors when a venue endpoint errors (best-effort, still 200)"*, i.e. it pinned serving an outage as an empty order book. A persist-test stub was also switched from a failing fetch to a succeeding one, or every assertion in that file would have passed for the wrong reason. Mutations: 3 on the tool wiring, 2 on the lib, 1 on the Discord copy — each red only its own assertion. Two mutations **survived** a first draft (a redundant null guard, and a null-ask sort case whose fixture could not observe it); the sort fixture was fixed and the guard documented as deliberately unreachable.

⚠ **NOT verified by HTTP round-trip** — the sandbox proxy blocks `rippackscity.com`. The production behaviour of the proxied Top Shot leg is inferred from the sibling callers that use the same `TS_PROXY_URL` pattern and are landing rows daily, not from a live request.

**Revert:** `git revert <sha>` — restores the old route, removes the tool, the lib module and the three new test files. **No DB change, no migration, no cron, no auth/`proxy.ts` change, no FMV/pricing math touched.** Note the persist path stays operator-gated and dormant either way, so `fmv_snapshots` is unaffected in both directions.

### 2026-08-15 · SHIPPED then REVERTED same session (Claude Code, interactive — followed the docs pass into the precompute defect) — the trust board's 999 failure sentinel is UNREACHABLE on a timeout; the obvious fix trades a bounded failure for an unbounded one

**What (net prod change: ZERO — applied, measured, reverted, verified):** three migrations,
`audit_20260815_thp_legs_catch_query_canceled` → `audit_20260815_thp_sentinel_helper_revoke_anon_auth`
→ `audit_20260815_revert_thp_legs_catch_query_canceled`. All eight `rpc_thp_leg_*` functions are back
on `EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS`, the helper `rpc_thp_sentinel_failures_since` is dropped, and
`rpc_trust_health_precompute_refresh_p()` is byte-restored. Verified after revert: 8/8 legs restored,
0 still carrying the change, 8/8 still SECURITY DEFINER, helper gone, procedure no longer references
it, `check_secdef_anon_exec_drift()` **0**, `check_public_security_invariants()` **0 rows**,
`check_anon_write_surface()` **0 rows**.

⚠ **The DEFECT is real and is now deliberately unfixed.** Every leg carries an `EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS`
handler that exists to write the **999 sentinel**, and PostgreSQL excludes `QUERY_CANCELED` from
`OTHERS`, which is exactly what `statement_timeout` raises (57014). Verified: `WHEN OTHERS` did NOT
catch a raised 57014; `WHEN query_canceled OR OTHERS` did; and `where value = 999` returns **zero rows,
ever**. So a timed-out leg writes neither its value nor its sentinel — it keeps the OLD value AND the
OLD `computed_at`, and aborts the CALL, skipping every downstream leg. `v_rpc_trust_health` shows no
per-metric age, so the board publishes a stale number as current. Only `trust_precompute_max_age_hours`
(breach 13, read 15.14) noticed.

⚠ **Why the fix was reverted — three measurements I did not have before applying:** (1) a
function-level `SET statement_timeout` does NOT bind statements inside it (300 ms declared,
`pg_sleep(5)` completed), so the legs' declared 60–480 s budgets are **all inert** — **second instance
of that trap today**, after `8918307c` on the drain seeders; (2) the real budget is `cron_heavy`'s
role-level **600 s shared by the whole CALL** — legs 1–7 burned **517 s**, leg 8 needed ~78 s and got
~83 s, so it is stalest **by position** and optimizing its query fixes nothing; (3) decisively, **after
a cancel is caught the timer is NOT re-armed** — probe at 500 ms, second `pg_sleep(3)` ran to
completion (`TAIL_UNBOUNDED ran_for=3.50s`). So catching buys a reachable sentinel at the price of
running every remaining leg **unbounded**, holding a connection on the 2 GB instance whose saturation
caused the timeout. plpgsql cannot re-arm mid-statement, so no in-procedure variant is safe.

⚠ **Security lesson, and it is the CONVERSE of the one already in CLAUDE.md:** `REVOKE EXECUTE … FROM
PUBLIC` alone was **not sufficient** — Supabase's `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES` grants EXECUTE to `anon` +
`authenticated` as explicit acl rows, so the new helper measured `has_function_privilege('anon', …) =
true` and drift went **0 → 1**. Fixed within minutes by revoking both halves. **The `proacl` text looked
clean** (the PUBLIC row really was gone) — which is why the rule is to verify with
`has_function_privilege()`.

⚠ **A name-trap nearly produced the opposite mechanism:** `rpc_trust_health_precompute_refresh` (FUNCTION,
13,009 chars, **zero callers anywhere**, `impossible_parallel` = leg **1**) vs
`rpc_trust_health_precompute_refresh_p` (PROCEDURE, 492 chars, the scheduled one, same leg = **8**).
**Read `cron.job.command`, not the name.**

**Real fix FILED, not taken** — 8 pg_cron entries instead of one orchestrator, so each leg gets its own
top-level statement and fresh budget:
`docs/overnight/inbox/2026-08-15T2240Z-the-999-sentinel-is-unreachable-on-a-timeout.md`.

**Revert:** already applied (`audit_20260815_revert_thp_legs_catch_query_canceled`). To re-apply the
forward change, re-run the first migration — but read measurement (3) first.

### 2026-08-15 · SHIPPED (Claude Code, interactive — "do everything mentioned") — wave 5 of 5: 8 block-scan indexers can silently skip blocks forever, and only 2 were tested for it

Allowlisting it would have been the per-file allowlist this repo keeps calling theatre. **What is forbidden is neither.**

### 2026-08-15 · SHIPPED (Claude Code, interactive) — the drain route's 20:30Z tick finally named the step, and the filed fix was aimed at the wrong thing

**What.** `drain-conflated-subeditions` has been killed at `maxDuration` on every tick since 2026-07-31. The 20:30Z tick today was the first to carry the progressive `mark()` from `80e99d4d`, and it settled it: `seed_miskeyed` **120,310 ms** · `seed_recent` **120,326 ms** · `seed_knot_occupants` **120,393 ms** (on a `p_limit` of **200**) · `seed_conflated` 16,946 ms · trigger 430 ms, `last_step = onchain_resolve_trigger`.

Three steps converging on ~120,3xx ms is a CEILING, not work. ⚠ **CORRECTED — WHICH ceiling is undetermined, and the attribution in the first version of this entry was wrong.** These functions do each declare `statement_timeout=120s` in `proconfig`, and I read that as binding because `service_role` carries 30s; but the **server default is ALSO exactly 120000 ms** (`/etc/postgresql-custom/platform-defaults.conf`, no db-level or `<ALL ROLES>` override), so the two are numerically indistinguishable. Prod controls say proconfig cannot RAISE the caller's budget, making the session default the likelier parent. **Raising these functions' proconfig would therefore do nothing** — the levers are the caller's budget or making the work fit, which is what this change does. A statement that hits it **rolls back** — so those three burned **361 s of a 600 s budget and produced nothing**, and the route was killed before reaching the steps that do the work.

Measured cost of that ordering: `resolve_topshot_subedition_collision_knots` (step 6) had **not executed once since 2026-07-31 20:33:53Z** — 76 resolutions ever, the newest stamped the exact minute of the last completed run, i.e. **15.0 days**, while knots arrive at ~+8.3/night (~124 accrued undrained).

**Fix — DRAIN before SEED, plus a wall-clock budget guard.** Order is now catalog → split → realign → **knots** → conflation_guard → seeds → on-chain trigger. The drain steps CONSUME what prior ticks resolved and the seeds FEED later ticks (the route header has always said so, and step 6 "derives its own candidates and does not read this queue"), so there is no intra-tick seed→drain dependency — the reorder changes throughput, never correctness, and every step is idempotent and cursor-driven. `knots` moved ahead of the conflation guard deliberately: the guard is a pure re-measurement and so is the cheapest thing to drop under pressure, and leaving knots last is exactly what let 15 days of starvation read as normal operation. No step may now START without room to hit its own 120 s ceiling and still write the completion row; a declined step lands in `extra.skipped_steps` rather than vanishing.

⚠ **This corrects the filed remedy.** Deep-audit R7 prescribed "split the 6 steps so each writes its own row and commits per step" — a large restructure of TopShot keying, the thing every edition-keyed FMV derives from — and it does not address the actual defect, which is that the three steps that time out ran FIRST and starved the rest. ⚠ R7's stated IMPACT was also wrong and is already corrected in Known issues #18: the conflation guard is **0.0 days stale** (it has a second caller, pg_cron jobid 62), so a session acting on R7 as filed would have fixed nothing.

**Guard.** `__tests__/pipeline-start-marker-duration-is-not-a-measurement.test.ts` gains an ordering pin — `knots` must precede every `seed_*` step, and `skipped_steps` must exist — because ordering here is load-bearing, not stylistic. Its existing `mark()`-call-site count was **repointed, not weakened**: it required >5 literal `mark(` sites, a proxy for "every step persists progress" that pinned the implementation; marking now lives inside the `step()` helper, which enforces the same property more strongly (a step cannot forget to mark) and reddened the guard on a correct refactor. Three mutations, each reddening only its own assertion: swapping `knots` behind the seeders, renaming `out.skipped_steps`, and dropping the `await` on `mark()`.

**Verified.** `tsc` clean · full primary suite **12,003 passed / 1,215 files**; the 4 failing files (7 tests: `api-ingest-backfill`, `metadata-catch-branch-is-not-a-404`, `worker-moments-hydrator-handler`, `worker-pack-events-ingest`) reproduce **identically at HEAD with these changes stashed**, so they are the documented local-env class, not this change. ⚠ Not verified by a live tick — the next 20:30Z run is the proof, and what to read is `extra.step_ms` plus a non-zero `knots` and a shrinking gap in `topshot_collision_knot_resolutions`.

**Revert:** `git revert 3a172b6b` (route + guard). No DB, migration, cron, auth, secret, hot-wallet or FMV/pricing-math change.

### 2026-08-15 · SHIPPED (Claude Code, interactive — "do everything mentioned") — wave 2 of 5: 7 DB pins on SCHEDULED WRITERS, chosen by measuring which prod-writing functions had no pin at all

- **Tests + 3 SNAPSHOT migrations, committed UNAPPLIED.** All three are byte-identical no-ops verified against live `prosrc` md5, so applying them buys nothing and costs a ~10–20 s burst of user-facing `PGRST002` 500s. No behaviour change, no cron change, no data mutation. Pins **132 → 139** over **131 → 138** distinct fns; `supabase/tests/*.sql` **130 → 137**.
- ⚠ **THE MEASUREMENT THAT PICKED THE TARGETS.** Live on 2026-08-15: **183 SECDEF functions in `public` WRITE** (insert/update/delete), **66 pinned (36%), 117 unpinned — and 25 of the unpinned ones run on an ACTIVE pg_cron schedule.** That is the least-covered high-stakes layer on the platform, and unlike the code gates nothing reports its coverage. Ranked by stakes, not by size.
- **The three DELETERS first, because a delete is the failure this layer cannot recover from** — over-deletion produces an ABSENCE, not an error, so nothing downstream reports it. `prune_pipeline_runs` (`41 */6 * * *`), `purge_candy_wmc_ghost_rows` (`10 9 * * *`), `prune_stale_wmc` (`20 10 * * 0`). None had a committed migration; all three now have one.
- **`purge_candy_wmc_ghost_rows` holds a deliberate opt-in past the destructive-op circuit breaker**, so the platform's backstop against a bulk `wallet_moments_cache` delete does not apply to it — **the pin is the only remaining check on what it deletes.** Its sharpest invariant is that the SURVIVOR is the newest row per `moment_id`: inverting the `ORDER BY` keeps the ghost and deletes the live owner, **with an identical row count either way**.
- **`prune_stale_wmc`'s 14-day bound appears TWICE and the copy inside the per-wallet DELETE is the load-bearing one** — without it a wallet that qualifies on ONE stale row loses its ENTIRE cache including moments seen minutes ago. Also pinned: the seeded exemption in BOTH directions (active exempt, **inactive NOT**), and that the per-wallet LOOP is a correctness requirement rather than a style choice (a set-based DELETE spanning >3 wallets is blocked at runtime by the circuit breaker).
- **Four more needed only a test** — `rollup_pipeline_runs`, `refresh_wmc_fmv_changed`, `public_board_liveness_sweep`, `refresh_unmapped_backlog_growth` already had committed migrations, all four verified byte-identical to live. **Worth checking before authoring a snapshot; it halved the work.**
- **`rollup_pipeline_runs`' MONOTONE GUARD is the best invariant in the set.** The oldest day in its re-aggregation window is being concurrently half-deleted by the pruner, so `WHERE EXCLUDED.runs >= d.runs` is what stops a pass overwriting a complete day with a truncated count — in the INDEFINITE archive that is the only pipeline history beyond ~73 h. The failure mode is a plausible smaller number.
- **Two pins are on INSTRUMENTS feeding arms that are breached right now** — `public_board_slow_count` and `unmapped_resolution_backlog_max`. A wrong instrument is worse than none: the SLOW-vs-EMPTY split decides whether the operator sees a perf problem or an outage, and `open_gross_unsplittable_rows` is exactly the "exclude on a permanent-failure REASON" the backlog arm's own text asks for.
- **All 43 mutations mutation-proven, and FOUR SURVIVED FIRST — every one taught something the test then encoded:**
  - ⚠ **A boundary test that is not ON the boundary asserts nothing.** `< → <=` survived because my fixture sat 1 second INSIDE the cutoff. `NOW()` is transaction-stable, so inserting `now() - interval '3 days'` lands exactly on `v_cutoff`.
  - ⚠ **An error-classification test needs a row that trips BOTH classifiers.** Collapsing SLOW/EMPTY survived because a raising board fails the slow test anyway (it errors in ~0 ms) — only a board that errors AND breaches `max_ms` distinguishes them.
  - ⚠ **`refresh_wmc_fmv_changed`'s three `fmv_usd IS NOT NULL` clauses are MUTUALLY REDUNDANT, measured not assumed.** Removing any ONE leaves the behaviour correct; removing any TWO still does; only all THREE blank a real price. No fixture can change that, so the test pins the BEHAVIOUR and says so — **and flags that removing two is the dangerous edit, individually harmless and leaving the portfolio value one edit from being wiped with the test still green.** I first wrote this up as "unreachable", which was wrong; the mutation matrix corrected me.
  - ⚠ **`wmc.edition_key IS NOT NULL` IS redundant** (the join already excludes NULL), documented as such with what would make it load-bearing again — a NULL-safe operator or a COALESCE on either side.
- **Verified:** local throwaway `postgres:16`, full DB suite **137 files / 0 failures**; drift guard + parser coverage **140 passed**; `tsc` clean.
- **Revert:** `git revert <sha>` — deletes the 7 SQL tests, the 3 snapshot migrations and the 7 PINS entries. **Nothing to unwind in the DB**: the migrations were never applied, and they are byte-identical to live in any case.

The pattern to watch for is that **a near-miss earns a comment, not a test** — and the comment is what makes it look handled.
- ⚠ **The second proven defect: `/[collection]/set/[slug]`'s `generateMetadata` catch could publish a failed read as `NOT_FOUND_METADATA` with `follow:false`, and nothing caught it.** Same mutation method, same result (green suite, green `tsc`). New guard `__tests__/metadata-catch-branch-is-not-a-404.test.ts`.
- ⚠ **Why the existing metadata guard could not see it — the guard-scope class again.** `metadata-failed-read-vs-absent-guard` is good and directory-driven, but fires only on bodies calling an **ok-carrying fetcher**. The five SEO entity pages carry no `ok` at all (their `fetchDetail` returns `T | null` and **throws**), so they were outside its scope by construction, however often it ran green.
- ⚠ **The rule is about `follow`, not `index`.** The repo already runs two robots vocabularies — `index:false, follow:FALSE` = "does not exist" (4 sites), `index:false, follow:TRUE` = "could not read it" (10 sites). A failed read may withhold indexing; it must never claim absence. Guard is spelling-independent (catches the inline form as well as the constant) and pins that the two vocabularies stay distinct.

### 2026-08-15 · SHIPPED (Claude Code, interactive) — a PUBLIC board told collectors "No +EV packs right now." out of its own 503, and a rewards read published "No referrals yet" from a failed count

- **Two code fixes + two tests.** No DB, no migration, no cron, no auth/`proxy.ts`, no FMV/pricing math.
- **Found by the method this repo documents rather than by reading fetch code:** sweep the empty-state COPY on client pages. `app/insights/pack-reality/page.tsx` is PUBLIC and its `error` state was consulted by **exactly ONE of five claim sites** (the pull-value distribution), so a 503 rendered "Failed to load: HTTP 503" in that section while **"No +EV packs right now."**, **"No qualifying packs yet."** and a hard **"0 positive-EV TS packs"** sat directly below it — the page contradicting itself, and the +EV ranker is a buy/no-buy input. Verified empirically with a throwaway probe before changing anything; all three strings confirmed present on a 503.
- ⚠ **THE EXISTING TEST DESCRIBED THE CONTRACT AND DID NOT ENFORCE IT.** `component-insights-client-pages-deep` already had a case whose comment read *"an outage must not render as 'no positive-EV packs exist right now', which is a claim about the market"* — and asserted only `toMatch(/HTTP 500|error|failed/i)`, i.e. that a failure was mentioned SOMEWHERE. Both can be true at once, and were. **Assert what the READER SEES, not that a failure was mentioned.** Same shape as the `f02362c7` panini case (asserted what the function returns, never what the reader sees).
- **Second instance, server-side and independent:** `/api/rewards/summary` returned `referralCount: referrals.count ?? 0`. **supabase-js RETURNS errors rather than throwing**, so a failed count (a `57014` statement timeout is the realistic case on this instance) yields `count: null` → a hard **0 at HTTP 200** → `/rewards` renders **"No referrals yet — be the first to share."** to a collector who may have referred friends and earned the credits. A claim about the reader's OWN account, same class as the `/alerts` fix. Now `null` end-to-end (the client's own `?? 0` would have undone it, and `InviteBlock`'s prop is typed nullable so a caller cannot pass a failed read as a zero).
- ⚠ **Both fixes pinned in BOTH directions, which is the load-bearing half.** An empty board and a genuinely-zero referral count are HONEST answers and must keep rendering as such — a fix that blanks every empty state into "unavailable" just moves the dishonesty and cries wolf on the system working. Mutation-proven: disabling `loadFailed` reds the board test and reproduces the original DOM verbatim; restoring `?? 0` reds the rewards test (`expected +0 to be null`).
- ⚠ **A mock bug nearly hid the second fix — my new test failed against an already-correct route.** The rewards suite's supabase stub returned a shared singleton from `from()`, and the route builds ~9 chains synchronously inside one `Promise.all`, so a single mutable `table` field was overwritten by every later `.from()` before any `then` settled — every chain resolved as the LAST table. `from()` now returns a builder closing over its own table. **A shared mutable builder cannot model per-table behaviour under `Promise.all`.**
- **Sibling checked, and it is clean:** `app/insights/allday-pack-reality` does not carry the same copy, so this did not spread by copy-paste the way the 15 OG cards and 5 sales indexers did.
- ✅ **Verified:** `tsc` clean · primary suite **11,961 passed / 1,211 files / 0 failures** · component gate **90.21 st / 81.76 br / 89.00 fn / 93.10 ln** against thresholds 89.8/81.3/88.6/92.7 (branch margin 0.46pt — the intended band, so no re-seat). ⚠ Not verified by HTTP round-trip: the sandbox proxy blocks `rippackscity.com` (documented 403 CONNECT).

### 2026-08-15 · SHIPPED (Claude Code, interactive) — two public deals views silently reverted to SECURITY DEFINER, because `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW` wipes reloptions and nothing about that is visible in a view's output

- **Prod DB change** (`audit_20260815_restore_security_invoker_on_deals_views`, committed as `supabase/migrations/20260815190500_…`) + a new repo guard `__tests__/migration-view-security-invoker-guard.test.ts`. No code, no cron, no data mutation.
- **What broke.** `check_public_security_invariants()` returned **2 rows** — `view_unexpected_definer` on `topshot_deals_vs_fmv` and `cross_collection_deals_board`. Cause found, not guessed: migration **`20260815153324`** (the deals-board partition-pruning win, applied 15:33Z today) recreated both with `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW … AS` and **no `WITH` clause**, which **RESETS reloptions** and dropped `security_invoker=on`. Timeline corroborates: night pass logged security 4/4 clean at 08:11Z, migration 15:33Z, monitor flagged exactly those two at 18:10Z.
- ⚠ **Mechanism verified EMPIRICALLY rather than asserted** — `create view pg_temp.zz with (security_invoker=on) as select 1;` → `security_invoker=on`; `create or replace view pg_temp.zz as select 1;` → **options GONE**.
- ⚠ **NOTHING IN THE AUTHORING LOOP COULD HAVE CAUGHT IT, and that is the whole finding.** That migration is a *good* one: it verified output **md5**, row count, buffer counts and `Subplans Removed`. **A view's security mode does not appear in its output**, so every one of those checks passes identically whether the view is invoker or definer. The defect is invisible to correctness testing by construction.
- ⚠ **NOTHING LEAKED — and I checked rather than accepting the monitor's "benign", which it had reached by ANALOGY to the Candy views.** That analogy does not hold: the Candy views had anon **revoked**, while these two are anon+authenticated SELECT **by design** (they back public `/insights/deals` + the concierge), so a definer view here really is an RLS-bypassing read. What makes it harmless is the *data*: every base table is catalog/market (`edition_offers`, `editions`, `fmv_snapshots`, `pinnacle_catalog`, `topshot_{thin_fmv,conflated}_editions`) with **no user-scoped rows**, so there was no per-user RLS to bypass. **The defect is lost hardening, not exposure.** Severity by measurement, not by precedent.
- ⚠ **`security_invoker=on` is the fix, NOT the allowlist — and the invariant says so itself.** Its arm-(b) comment reads *"catches a hardened (invoker) view silently reverting to definer"*. Allowlisting would have **accepted the exact regression the arm exists to detect**. ⚠ Verified invoker was SAFE before applying: anon holds SELECT on every base table and every policy admits it (`USING (true)`, `editions` scoped to active collections, `collections` `is_active`).
- ⚠ **`ALTER VIEW`, not `CREATE OR REPLACE`** — it touches only the catalog entry, so the repair cannot drift the query definition as a side effect, which is the failure being repaired. Both views in ONE migration, since each `apply_migration` costs a ~10–20 s burst of user-facing `PGRST002` 500s.
- ✅ **Verified after apply, including the half that regresses by SILENCE.** Invariants **2 → 0**, `check_anon_write_surface()` 0, both views read `security_invoker=on`, `secdef_drift` 0, `rls_off` 0. The public board re-fetched **anonymously end-to-end** returns 50/50 rows, the **identical row set** to the pre-change baseline, and all three legs (`nba_top_shot`, `nfl_all_day`, `disney_pinnacle`). **A broken invoker view fails by returning NOTHING, so a clean invariant alone would not have been evidence the board still worked.**
- ⚠ **MY FIRST VERSION OF THAT CHECK WAS SERVED BY THE EDGE CACHE AND PROVED NOTHING — I caught it on the numbers.** "Byte-identical, 30,856 bytes" also carried an **`elapsed_ms` identical to the millisecond (5833 both times)**, which no independent execution produces. I had compared a cached response to itself. Re-run with a cache-busting query param (a distinct cache key), the board genuinely re-executes — 30,856 B, `elapsed_ms` **5455**, same row set. ⚠ **A byte-identical result is the signature of a cache hit at least as much as of a correct change**, and on a route that sets a public `s-maxage` that is the likelier reading; carry a per-request nonce when verifying a write against a cached read.
- ⚠ **That cache-busted run also produced a 503 on 1 of 2 requests — pre-existing, and I proved it rather than waving at it.** Body is `code:"timeout", retryable:true` (the `boardUnavailable` classification), and `deals` is filed at a **59.5%** tick-failure rate on `cross_collection_deals_board: canceling statement due to statement timeout`. **My change cannot be the cause**: the route reads via `supabaseAdmin` (⚠ imported as `import { supabaseAdmin as supabase }` — the documented "an identifier named `supabase` is usually the service-role client" trap, checked rather than assumed), and **`service_role` carries `rolbypassrls = true`**, so under invoker mode the view still executes with RLS bypassed and **no policy predicate is added to the plan**. Invoker is a no-op for the app path's cost; only a true anon PostgREST read would pay it.
- ⚠ **THE DURABLE PART: this is the FOURTH occurrence, and every previous one was documented INSIDE the migration that caused it — where the next author never looks.** `v_rpc_trust_health` carries *"THE ALTER VIEW BELOW IS LOAD-BEARING … this exact view silently lost `security_invoker=on` that way"*; `panini_squeeze_board` carries *"this migration dropped security_invoker as a side effect, repaired minutes later by …"*; and **`20260801012254` creates TWO views, re-asserts the option for `v_topshot_pack_market` and forgets `pack_ev_latest`, though its own header says it meant to do both.** The knowledge existed and was unreachable. Hence a guard: `CREATE [OR REPLACE] VIEW public.X` in a migration must state a security mode for **that view** — inline `WITH (security_invoker = on)` **or** a matching `ALTER VIEW X SET (…)`, the repo's established convention. **Keyed per VIEW NAME on purpose**, because "a file that hardens view A vouches for view B" is not hypothetical — it is `pack_ev_latest`.
- ⚠ **My first version of the guard was WRONG and the migrations corrected it.** I sized it with a per-FILE grep (`does the file mention security_invoker`), got 88% compliance, and wrote a per-STATEMENT check — which then red-flagged ~20 legitimate files using the `ALTER VIEW` convention. **The convention was right and my rule was wrong**; per-file also *undercounted*, hiding the five files that mention the option for a different view. Both errors came from one shortcut: measuring at file granularity a property that lives on a statement.
- **16 files grandfathered, each checked LIVE rather than excused as old:** `pack_ev_latest` is definer **but allowlisted with anon SELECT revoked** (accepted by design, no exposure), `panini_squeeze_board` and `pinnacle_unresolved_with_owner` are invoker/allowlisted. Applied migrations are history — editing them cannot change production, since they are never re-run — so the repair is a NEW migration, and a guard case pins that (editing the applied file would turn the guard green while prod stayed definer). **The list is size-pinned so it cannot grow silently.**
- **Mutation-proven in three directions:** a new unguarded `CREATE VIEW` → caught; the same hardened via `ALTER VIEW` → passes (no false positive on the real convention); **two views with only one hardened → catches exactly the unhardened one**, reproducing the `pack_ev_latest` shape. Guard strips SQL comments first — required, since the repair migration quotes `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW public.topshot_deals_vs_fmv` in its own header (this repo's recurring trap, now on its fifth instance).
- **Verified:** `tsc` clean; guard + `proxy-is-public-path` **165 passed**.
- **Revert:** `ALTER VIEW public.topshot_deals_vs_fmv SET (security_invoker = off);` + same for `cross_collection_deals_board` — **which re-opens the invariant breach; prefer fixing forward.** `git revert <sha>` drops the guard + the committed migration file (the DB stays hardened either way).

### 2026-08-15 · SHIPPED (Claude Code, interactive) — the auth wall does not stand for any path ending in a static extension; a fix diagnosed two days earlier had sat on disk, unpushed. ⚠ DEFENSE-IN-DEPTH, NOT A BREACH — and the severity I first wrote here was disproved by a control test

Replaced with **`STATIC_ROOT_ASSETS`, an exact `Set`** of the 7 real root assets. `proxy.ts` + `__tests__/proxy-is-public-path.test.ts`. No DB, migration, cron, hot-wallet or FMV change.
- ⚠ **THE FINDING IS NOT THE BUG — IT IS THAT THE FIX EXISTED AND NOBODY SHIPPED IT.** A 2026-08-13 cloud session diagnosed this, verified it against production, wrote the patch, the tests, a handoff and a paste-ready ledger entry — and could not push (`/sessions` disk full). Everything was on disk, gitignored (`*.patch`), invisible to `git status` except as two stray untracked docs. `proxy.ts` on `main` still carried the vulnerable line. **A fix that cannot be pushed is not a fix, and a handoff describing one reads exactly like a shipped one three days later.** The `docs/session-close-2026-08-13-cowork-cloud.md` header — "Ended with a live production auth bypass closed **on paper**" — was accurate and got read as a completion.
- ✅ **THE BYPASS IS REAL, on evidence that survives a control.** Anonymously, `GET /api/mcp/keys/<uuid>` → **307 → `/login`** while `GET /api/mcp/keys/<uuid>.png` → **405 Method Not Allowed**. **A 405 cannot come from the auth wall** — the wall's answer is the 307 — so the suffixed request reached the handler. Verified live here, independently of the collection pages.
- ⛔ **AND MY OWN HEADLINE EVIDENCE WAS WRONG, in exactly the way the inherited one was — a concurrent session caught it mid-flight (`5043f09f`) and re-measuring agreed.** I reported `GET /profile/edit` → 307 vs `GET /profile/edit.css` → **200, 29,789 bytes of HTML** as proof the wall had been bypassed onto a gated page. **It is not.** The suffixed path routes to `/profile/[username]` — **public by design** — with `username = "edit.css"`; the rendered `h1` is literally `edit.css`. The 08-13 report's `/topshot.png` claim fails the same way — the next hop is `/[collection]/overview`, public since the 2026-07-17 un-gate.
