I had already corrected an inherited wrong test row using a positive control an hour earlier and still did not run the equivalent control on my own headline claim: **a control is not a step you do once, it is what makes any comparative claim mean anything.**

### 2026-08-15 · ⚠ PROD DB CHANGE (Claude Code, interactive) — `pinnacle_fmv_history` stops dropping the ASK_ONLY revision; a Pinnacle page no longer contradicts its own chart

- **Migration `audit_20260815_pinnacle_fmv_history_keep_last_write_per_timestamp` (version `20260815172945`), committed as `supabase/migrations/20260815172945_*.sql`. ONE `CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION` on a trigger — no data rewritten, no schema change, no code.**
- ⚠ **REVERT:** re-run that migration file with `DO UPDATE SET …` replaced by `DO NOTHING`.
- **The defect:** `pinnacle_fmv_recalc_render_all()` writes each render **twice in ONE transaction** — the sales loop, then the ASK_ONLY pass (`fmv_usd = floor_ask*0.90`). **`NOW()` is transaction-stable**, so both stamp the same `fmv_computed_at`, the second trigger firing collided on `(render_id, computed_at)`, and `DO NOTHING` **threw the published value away**. Measured **715 of 2,480** priced rows (776 when first found), split exactly — HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW/STALE **0**, ASK_ONLY **all of them** — max divergence **$2,974.47**. `get_edition_fmv_history` reads that table, so a Pinnacle edition page plotted a series whose latest point was **not the FMV shown on the same page**.
- ⚠ **The safety check that made `DO UPDATE` defensible, done BEFORE applying** — otherwise it could overwrite genuine historical points. Only **two** writers touch `pinnacle_catalog`: `pinnacle_catalog_set_floor_asks` **never references `fmv_usd`**, so the trigger's WHEN clause cannot fire for it; and the recalc **always** sets `fmv_computed_at = NOW()`. No code-side writer exists either (repo swept). So a conflict on that key can ONLY mean "same render, same recalc transaction" — exactly the case being fixed.
- **VERIFIED AGAINST THE ACTUAL BUG, not just applied:** forced the exact double-write (two UPDATEs to one render in one transaction sharing a `computed_at`) inside a **rolled-back subtransaction**; history kept the **second/published** value, and a residue check found **0 rows** in `pinnacle_catalog` and `pinnacle_fmv_history`.
- ⚠ **FORWARD-ONLY BY DESIGN — the 715 existing wrong rows are NOT rewritten.** Rewriting historical price records is a data mutation with no need: the next recalc writes a fresh row at a new timestamp, so each render's **latest** point — the one that contradicts the page — self-corrects on the next run, within ~12 h at the current cadence.
- **Applied in a verified quiet window**: `pg_stat_activity` had dropped to **3 backends / oldest 73 s** from the earlier **15 / 486 s**, so the ~10–20 s `PGRST002` schema-cache burst every migration costs landed when the instance could absorb it.

- ⚠ **THE HEADLINE — the proposed durable fix is REFUTED, and I refuted it by building it.** `aggregate_saved_wallet_stats` computes `top_tier` with a **correlated subquery per collection_id** on top of its group scan, which reads as the obvious N+1 to eliminate. I wrote the single-pass replacement (`array_agg(… ORDER BY tier_rank) FILTER (…)[1]`, one scan, no correlated subquery) and measured it on a stuck wallet: **73,983 ms for 14,260 rows**, `Buffers: shared hit=1183 read=11457` — a **9% cache hit ratio**. Rewriting a live pinned DB function would have shipped churn and fixed **nothing**. *A cost estimate is not a measurement, and the obvious N+1 is not always the cost.*

(b) **"Commit per-wallet rather than one large UPDATE" is ALREADY DONE** — that internal COMMIT is precisely what 2D000 exposes. The failure is a *single wallet's* aggregation blowing the statement budget, not one large UPDATE.

- **Also landed this session:** the stranded 15:10Z daytime monitor, committed from the mount (shell down ~8th day).

### 2026-08-15 · SHIPPED (Claude Code, interactive — "do all of these", cont.) — ⚠ USER-FACING: /alerts told a collector "No alerts yet" and "not linked" off a FAILED read; + re-seated the component ratchet

- **The defect.** `app/alerts/page.tsx` ran three fetches under one `Promise.all`, guarded each with `if (res.ok)`, and on a `!ok` response simply **left state at its initial `[]`** — with a bare `catch { /* ignore */ }` swallowing a thrown fetch outright. Every claim on that page is about the reader's **OWN account**, which makes it the sharpest instance of this class after the dashboard hero-picker:
  - **"No alerts yet. Create one above."** — actively invites a **DUPLICATE** of an alert the collector already has.
  - **"No watched editions yet."**
  - the channel list rendered every channel **"not linked"** with a Link button — telling someone whose Telegram IS linked that it is not, and inviting a re-link.
- **Found by sweeping client-page empty-state copy**, not from a report. `app/**/page.tsx` is measured by NEITHER coverage gate (44,413 LOC), so nothing was ever going to surface this automatically.
- **Fix.** Per-leg failure tracking (`{channels, subs, fmv}`) rather than one flag — the three endpoints fail independently and a single flag would blank all three sections whenever any one broke. Failure branch **precedes** the empty branch (ordering is what makes it non-inert); the empty-state copy is **KEPT**, because owning nothing is still a real answer; the thrown-fetch path fails **all three** legs, since one `Promise.all` means no leg's state can be trusted. The channels leg gets a notice above the list instead — there is no empty state there, the false claim IS the per-channel status.
- **Guard:** extended `__tests__/client-pages-failed-vs-empty-guard.test.ts` (2 sites → 3), 5 mutations, all killed. No failure message diagnoses a cause it cannot know — the defect these replace was a confident wrong explanation, and new copy that guesses differently would be the same mistake in new words.

The branch buffer had drifted to **2.34pt**, the same direction as the ~13pt incident this file records — no coverage was added by this pass, it is purely putting the ratchet back under the actuals it exists to protect. Margins now ~0.4–0.5pt, matching the primary gate.
- **Verified:** `tsc` clean; guard 10/10; component gate green at the RAISED thresholds (1,680 tests).
- **Revert:** `git revert <sha>`. No DB change.

### 2026-08-15 · SHIPPED (Claude Code, interactive — "do all of these") — ⚠ USER-FACING: six public OG cards published a CAPPED PAGE LENGTH as a board total; top-sales said "3 sales this week" against 30,592

- **The defect.** Every `/api/public/insights/**` route published `meta.total_rows: data?.length ?? 0` — the length of the CAPPED page (each route clamps `limit` via `Math.min`), under a name that means the opposite. Six OG cards read it as a board total, and **three read it off the same `limit=3` request they used to render their top-3 rows**. Measured live 2026-08-15:
  | card | published | true |
  |---|---|---|
  | `top-sales` | **"3 sales this week"** | **30,592** |
  | `serial-premiums` | "3 editions tracked" | — |
  | `underpriced-serials` | "3 live deals" | — |
  | `squeeze` | "200 editions squeezed 50%+" | 1,352 |
  | `trophies` | "500 grails ranked" | 842 |
- ⚠ **It was the NAME, not the arithmetic.** A consumer reading `total_rows` has no reason to suspect a page length. And an OG card is a static, edge-cached PNG only ever seen in *someone else's* timeline — so these were simultaneously the most wrong and the least observable numbers on the platform. Same family as the documented "silently sliced ranking": every row shown is correct, the board just stops, and the number attached is presented as a census.
- **Fix.** `lib/insights/board-meta.ts` adds `returned_rows` + `truncated` beside `total_rows` (**kept unchanged** — the concierge's `fetchPublicInsight` and external consumers read it). `lib/og/board-count.ts` does ONE count request at each route's own max limit and renders a **floor** (`"200+"`) when the read was capped. ⚠ Deliberately **not** fixed with `count: exact` — these are anon endpoints on a 2 GB disk-IO-throttled instance where the insights refresher already fails 4 of 6 board warms per tick; a full count per request would buy a nicer number by worsening the saturation that causes the timeouts.
- ⚠ **A broader guard was tried and REJECTED after measuring — it flagged four CORRECT cards.** "Any card publishing a count must use the helper" reds `pack-drops` (uncapped fetch), `pack-sniper` (`positiveEv` counted before the `slice(0, limit)`), `set-completers` (route has no limit) and `rookies` (a real cohort aggregate). Forcing those through the helper would have **replaced four exact counts with floors — making accurate cards less accurate to satisfy a guard.** The rejected rule and the four verifications are recorded in the test file so nobody re-derives it.
- **Guard:** `__tests__/og-insights-headline-count-is-not-a-page-length.test.ts` — directory-driven over the whole `og/insights` tree, strips comments first, and mutation-proven. ⚠ It matches the **call forms** `boardCountLabel(` / `fetchBoardCount(`, not the bare identifiers: a card that keeps the import while hand-rolling the interpolation satisfies a plain `includes()` and slips through (caught by mutation, not by review).
- **Also:** `allday-scarcity` / `pinnacle-scarcity` read `total_rows` purely as a non-empty gate (they print "· live", no number) — re-pointed at `rows.length`, which is the honest expression and keeps the guard strict. Three now-dead count-only second fetches removed; `underpriced-serials`' second fetch **kept** (it also refills rows).
- **Verified:** full gate **11,866 passed** (+42), 91.65 st / 78.97 br; `tsc` clean; all 28 public-insights route suites green. ⚠ **Not verified by HTTP round-trip** — the sandbox proxy blocks `rippackscity.com` (documented 403 CONNECT).
- **Revert:** `git revert <sha>`. No DB change, no migration.

- **The Candy views have NOTHING TO FIX.** `candy_pack_market` reads 2,501 + 387 + 332 rows plus a planner-cost-292 view — a **~2.5 MB working set** — and measured **128.8 s**. No plan defect explains that ratio. Anyone sent there by the `public_board_slow_count` breach will find nothing.

That is the documented burst-credit model at depletion — throttled to the ~22 MB/s baseline with all reads queued. **Disk-IO-bound, not compute-bound.**
- **So the board timeouts, the entity-page pool-acquire family, the `fmv-recalc` kill rate and the Candy 128 s are the SAME condition from four surfaces.** The only lever that works is **reducing total disk-read volume** — which is what actually moved things this week (the `deals` pruning −30.4% buffers, the 113 GB backfill re-scoping, the 27 GB/day telemetry sampling, the 72 MB index drop). Per-query tuning on already-cheap views does not.
- ⚠ **METHOD NOTE — I was part of the problem.** Diagnosing this cost `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE)` runs of 42 s, 30 s, 7 s and 4.7 s against the same starved instance. **On a burst-credit database, profiling IS load.** Batch measurements, prefer `EXPLAIN` without `ANALYZE` and `pg_class.reltuples` over `count(*)`, and stop when the instance starts refusing trivial queries instead of pressing on. I stopped rather than continuing.
- **DELIBERATELY DEFERRED, not forgotten:** the `pinnacle_fmv_history` ASK_ONLY migration (`inbox/2026-08-15T0620Z-…`) is ready and small, but **every `apply_migration` costs a ~10–20 s burst of user-facing `PGRST002` 500s**, and firing that at an instance already failing trivial reads would be the wrong trade. ### 2026-08-15 · SHIPPED (Claude Code, interactive — "keep going, use your judgement") — the fmv-recalc "runs halved" mystery is SOLVED: it is not running less, it is being KILLED, and the instrument that says otherwise was measuring itself

- **Code + tests + docs, direct to `main`. Two routes touched, both TELEMETRY-ONLY inserts — no FMV/pricing math, no DB, no migration, no cron, no auth/`proxy.ts`, no hot-wallet change.** Drains deep-audit run-2 item on `drain-conflated-subeditions` (re-pointed, see below) and closes the open `fmv-recalc` diagnosis.
- **Revert:** `git revert <sha>` — code/tests/docs only, nothing to unwind in the DB.
- ⚠ **THE FIND, and it corrects THIS FILE'S OWN claim from earlier today.** CLAUDE.md said fmv-recalc's 08-14 run-count halving (93 → 41) was "NOT explained by the failure rate — fewer runs were *started*". Wrong: **`pipeline_runs` counts SURVIVORS, not invocations.** fmv-recalc writes its terminal row at the END, so a run killed at the 300 s cap writes *nothing* — it is not a failure, it vanishes. Running the NOT-EXISTS correlation the route's own `fmv-recalc-heartbeat` documents: **08-12 141 invocations / 38.3% killed · 08-13 162 / 42.6% · 08-14 165 / 75.2% · 08-15 109 / 63.3%.** **Total invocations are FLAT — the scheduler never changed; the COMPLETION rate collapsed.** One regression (saturation), not two.
- ⚠ **Killed runs still do real work and record none of it**, so `pipeline_runs_daily.rows_written` undercuts actual repricing by roughly the kill rate — 10,684 on 08-14 is survivors' output only, not total throughput.
- ⚠ **Nothing watches this: the kill-detection query exists only as a COMMENT.** Cadence monitors structurally cannot see it (the cron fires perfectly; the work inside dies), which is why the visible symptom — a halved run count — reads as a *scheduling* problem and sends you to the wrong place.
- ⚠ **SHIPPED — a start marker was publishing its own INSERT LATENCY as the run's duration.** `pipeline_runs.duration_ms` is `GENERATED ALWAYS AS (finished_at - started_at)` and `finished_at` is `NOT NULL DEFAULT now()`, so any marker omitting `finished_at` emits a plausible-looking number that measures the telemetry write. **This already cost a wrong diagnosis**: deep-audit run 2 read drain-conflated-subeditions' 147/176/185 ms as the route "dying instantly" when it is running to its ceiling and being killed — the opposite conclusion, pointing at a different fix. Both writers now pin `finished_at = started_at` → hard **0**, an obvious sentinel. Blast radius was larger than the audit's 3 rows: **514 `fmv-recalc-heartbeat` rows** publishing 42 ms–56 s of pure insert cost.
- **Guard added** (`__tests__/pipeline-start-marker-duration-is-not-a-measurement.test.ts`, 4 tests): **scans for the marker pattern rather than naming files**, so a new marker writer is covered the day it lands — and it immediately found the second instance (`fmv-recalc`) that I had not spotted by reading. Mutation-proven: dropping `finished_at` from the drain marker reds exactly 1.
- ⚠ **One deliberate loss, recorded:** the 56 s marker-insert outlier was incidental evidence of connection-acquire saturation, but it was unlabelled and **indistinguishable from a run duration**, which is the whole harm. Measure insert latency deliberately into `extra` if it is wanted.
- ⚠ **Corrected a second claim of my own:** CLAUDE.md implied fmv-recalc cursor progress is unmeasurable because `extra` has no cursor keys. True of `extra`, but `cursor_before`/`cursor_after` are real COLUMNS, populated 201/201 and 194/201 with 157 advancing. **Read the columns.**
- **NOT taken (needs a lane I stayed out of):** making the kill rate observable (a TRACK-only metric over the existing correlation, then a trust arm — calibrate on the KILL RATE, not the run count), and making runs fit inside 300 s (page size per invocation = FMV pipeline tuning). ⚠ **Do not raise `maxDuration`** — 800 s is a hard cap whose breach ERRORs the deploy invisibly, and a longer run holds a pooled connection longer on the instance that is already the bottleneck. Filed: `inbox/2026-08-15T1600Z-…`.

- **Docs only on `main`. One `UPDATE` against prod was attempted and REJECTED by a foreign key — zero rows written, nothing to unwind.** Read-only investigation otherwise.

- ⚠ **THE PART WORTH REMEMBERING — the data looked bridgeable, I wrote the heal, and a FOREIGN KEY refused it.** 307 of the 329 are in `pinnacle_mint_events`, all with a non-null `edition_id` across 114 editions — which reads exactly like a one-line fill-only repair. But **`pinnacle_mint_events.edition_id` is a NUMERIC Pinnacle edition id (`2490`) while `pinnacle_sales.edition_id` is the TEXT edition_key (`STAR-OEV1-MAND:Silver Sparkle:1`)** with an FK to `pinnacle_editions`. Two vocabularies under one column name — the same class as the platform's long-form/short-form collection footgun. The statement aborted whole; **had the FK not existed I would have written 307 numeric ids into a text edition_key column and silently corrupted the join for every Pinnacle surface.** Do NOT relax that constraint.
- **Actual root cause: a grain gap, not a pipeline.** Of the 114 numeric editions behind these sales, **0 exist in `pinnacle_editions` (547 rows) and 114 exist in `pinnacle_catalog` (2,561 rows)**. `pinnacle_sales.edition_id` can only reference `pinnacle_editions`, so a sale of a catalog-only edition is **structurally unresolvable**.
- ⚠ **And the "clean onset" is a red herring.** Those editions' catalog rows were created **06-06 → 08-12** — they are not new. 08-14 16:00Z is when they started TRADING (13 distinct sets). A pre-existing coverage gap surfaced through a shift in the trading mix; nothing changed in our pipelines that hour.

That table is the **render-keyed FMV** surface — inserting 114 rows changes what the FMV recompute, the scarcity board and the serial-multiplier model consider to exist, and Pinnacle FMV joins must use the `(character_name, set_name, variant_type)` triple. That is an ingest/pricing project with a review, precisely the lane kept off the autonomous path.

### 2026-08-15 · SHIPPED (Claude Code, interactive, cont.) — drained four more deep-audit items: a confused deputy, two failure-renders-as-data sites, the site-wide unfurl byline, and a committed credential workflow

- **Code + tests, direct to `main`. No DB, no migration, no cron, no hot-wallet, no FMV/pricing-MATH change.** Second wave on deep-audit run 2 — **R13**, **R12**, **R10**, **R16**. Everything mutation-proven; both gates green.
- ⚠ **R13 (P2) — `/api/profile/achievements` POST was a CONFUSED DEPUTY.** It read `ownerKey` from the request **body** and then called the compute-achievements edge function with the **server's `INGEST_SECRET_TOKEN`**, with no ownership check — so a caller could make RPC recompute and WRITE achievements for an arbitrary `owner_key` using our own operator credential. Every sibling `/api/profile/**` writer already carries `requireOwnedKey`; this one was missed. Now gated, fails closed on 401/403/any resolution error, and the test asserts **the edge fetch is never reached** — the credential must not be spent before the gate.
- **R13's other half — GET returned `{achievements: []}` at HTTP 200 on a Postgres error.** Byte-identical to "you have unlocked nothing", so an outage silently erased a collector's achievements from their own profile. ⚠ **Invisible to BOTH driver-message leak guards by construction** — it swallowed the message entirely, and a guard that hunts for leaked text finds nothing in a response that leaks nothing. Now `apiErrorResponse`. ⚠ **The GET's missing ownership check is deliberately NOT a finding and is now commented as such:** `profile_achievements` carries an explicit `"public read achievements"` RLS policy (`roles={public}, qual=true`), so those rows are already anon-readable — adding a gate would imply a privacy property the table does not have.
- ⚠ **Two existing tests were titled *"swallows a DB error into { achievements: [] }"*** — a title that makes the defect read as the contract, the same shape this repo has now hit repeatedly. Rewritten to assert the property (failure reported as failure, driver text absent), plus a **positive mirror** so a genuinely empty set is still an honest `200 []`.
- **R12 (P2) — `/share/<wallet>` rendered a failed read as *"We haven't indexed this wallet yet"*.** `fetchSnapshot` returned a bare `null` for both "the read failed" and "this wallet holds nothing" — a claim about OUR INDEX manufactured from a transient failure, on the page a collector deliberately shares. ⚠ **Worse than a wording bug: that empty state QUEUES the wallet for indexing and polls**, so an outage spent real ingest work re-indexing wallets that were never the problem. Now returns `{ data, ok }` and a failed read renders a distinct `ShareUnavailable` that queues nothing.
- **R12 also emitted no canonical** — `/share/0xABC` and `/share/0xabc` are the same card at two indexable URLs, and this page is shared BY HAND so both spellings really occur. Canonicalised on the lowercase form.
- **R10 (P2) — the `openGraph`/`twitter` shallow-merge trap was live in all three shared `lib/seo.ts` helpers.** Next merges page metadata into the root at the TOP-LEVEL key only, so defining `openGraph` in a child **replaces** the root block outright and every omitted field vanishes. Coverage: `pageMetadata` (~40 tab URLs), `buildMeta` (the whole entity corpus, ~23.5k editions), `collectionLayoutMetadata` (5 roots). Visible symptom: **the public boards the concierge calls "the most shareable thing RPC has" unfurled with no X byline at all.** `app/profile/[username]/layout.tsx` had documented the trap and got it right; the fix was never generalised.
- **The R10 guard DERIVES its field list from `rootMetadata` rather than restating it**, so adding a field at the root widens the guard automatically instead of leaving a new hole — and it carries a not-vacuous check plus a reverse assertion that per-page titles are not flattened by the shared spread. ⚠ `buildMeta` is **private**, so it is exercised through `editionPageMetadata`, a real public caller — testing the export surface, not an implementation detail.
- **R16 (P3) — `scripts/local-cost-basis-backfill.mjs` shipped `PASTE_FRESH_COOKIES_HERE` / `PASTE_FRESH_X_ID_TOKEN_HERE` as committed constants**, i.e. a tracked file whose documented workflow is "edit these two credentials in place". That is exactly the workflow whose leak forced the 2026-08-03 `git filter-repo` + force-push that rewrote every pre-purge sha in this repo. Now reads `DAPPER_COOKIE` / `DAPPER_X_ID_TOKEN` from the environment and exits 1 with an explicit "do NOT edit them into this file" message; both documented in `.env.example`.

### 2026-08-14 · SHIPPED (Claude Code, interactive, cont.) — read `rpc_search_catalog` instead of inferring, and had to CORRECT my own narrative-search diagnosis: it is a flat flag, not a length-normalized score

- **Docs only, direct to `main`. No code, no DB, no migration, no prod-state change.** ⚠ No Vercel deploy expected (`ignoreCommand` skips `*.md`).
- ⚠ **MY OWN FILED DIAGNOSIS WAS PARTLY WRONG, and I only found out by reading the function.** I had written that matches are ranked by trigram `similarity()` which is "length-normalized, so a long paragraph scores below a short set name". **There is no paragraph score.** The edition arm computes similarity against **names only** (`player_name || set_name`); the description's ENTIRE contribution is a flat boolean `CASE WHEN via_prose THEN 0.12`. I had inferred a mechanism from behaviour and filed it as fact.
- **The measured mechanism.** `121:4255`, whose description literally contains "buzzer", scores **0.1404**. **Buddy Hield — a fuzzy NAME match with no prose match at all — scores 0.4676.** A verbatim prose containment loses **3×** to a name resemblance, because a player hit also collects the 0.35 kind-weight while a prose hit collects 0.12. And because the boost is FLAT, every prose hit scores identically, so within them the effective order is the tiebreak `u.lbl ASC` — **alphabetical**. That is why the moment is unreachable even at limit 50: not outranked by one thing, buried in a mass of ties.
- ⚠ **TWO hypotheses tested and REJECTED, recorded so nobody re-derives them.** (1) **Candidate truncation** — `edition_hits` ends `ORDER BY circulation_count ASC LIMIT 200`, a relevance-blind pre-filter that looked damning; **rejected by measurement**: 297 editions match "buzzer", the target's circulation is 28, only **13** sort ahead of it, so it is comfortably inside the 200. (2) **"Set names outrank prose"** — directionally true for one query but not the mechanism, and believing it hid the real one; here a *player* name did the outranking.
- **A SECOND, distinct defect separated out.** `48:1652` is not ranked low for `game winner`, it is **excluded entirely**: `LIKE ALL` demands every token and its description says **"game-winning"**, which `'%winner%'` does not match. So the two Lillard moments fail for **different reasons** — one ranking, one tokenization — and any fix claiming to solve narrative search must address both and be verified against BOTH slugs.
- **Design specified with its regression named:** a graded, **exclusivity-gated** prose contribution (phrase-in-description AND phrase-NOT-in-any-name-field → strong boost; all-tokens → moderate). ⚠ The gate is load-bearing: a naive "+0.55 whenever description matches" **regresses ordinary name search** — querying `lillard` would lift every edition whose prose mentions him to ~0.85, level with the Lillard PLAYER hit, so searching a player could stop returning that player first. Stemming still needs FTS (`tsvector` + `ts_rank`); `editions` is only ~27k rows, so that is cheap.
- **Why I did NOT ship it:** live ranking behind BOTH the public header search and the concierge's `search_catalog`, and the regression it risks is exactly the kind that passes a spot check and needs a broad before/after battery written first. The investigation is done; what remains is verification breadth.
- **Revert:** `git revert <sha>` — documentation only.

### 2026-08-14 · SHIPPED (Claude Code, interactive, cont.) — figured out BOTH open items without an operator: the walker query was already proven, and the All Day 403 is a one-line env change

- **Code comments + inbox filing, direct to `main`. No DB, no migration, no cron, no auth/`proxy.ts`, no hot-wallet, no FMV/pricing-MATH change.** Both open items from the previous wave resolved by reading evidence already in hand rather than asking for a curl.
- ⚠ **ITEM 1 — the walker's 422 risk was ALREADY DISPROVEN and I had asked for a redundant verification.** The 2026-08-13 probe ran `searchEditions` → `play { stats { <field> } }` against live Top Shot and returned **sample VALUES** for all three new fields (`birthdate` `"1999-06-17"`, `birthplace` `"Havre De Grace, MD, USA"`, `draftYear` `2020`). A sample value means the query VALIDATED AND EXECUTED. The walker uses the **same endpoint, same operation, same `SearchEditionsInput!`, same nesting** — and GraphQL selection is ADDITIVE, so adding already-valid fields to an already-valid selection set cannot invalidate it. **The verification curl I asked for was unnecessary.** Worth recording: "I cannot test this" was false; the test had already been run for a different purpose.
- ⚠ **ITEM 2 — the All Day WAF 403 is a ROUTE problem with a one-line fix.** Read `workers/topshot-proxy/index.js`: only **`/allday-consumer`** carries `ROUTE_HEADERS` (`Origin: nflallday.com`, `Referer`, browser UA) — exactly the fingerprint a Cloudflare WAF checks. **`/allday` sends the bare `sports-collectible-tool/0.1` UA with no Origin**, and `lib/editions-hydrate.ts` sends no Origin either. The README sets `ALLDAY_PROXY_URL` to the worker's **`/allday`** route. **Suggested fix: point it at `/allday-consumer`** — which is right for TWO independent reasons: the fingerprint, AND that `allEditions` (used by both the probe arm and editions-hydrate) belongs to the **consumer** endpoint, which is that route's upstream and editions-hydrate's own `ALLDAY_GQL_DEFAULT`. If `ALLDAY_PROXY_URL` is currently `/allday`, the query is going to the WRONG ENDPOINT independent of the WAF.
- ⚠ **AND I NEARLY SHIPPED A WRONG INFERENCE, caught by re-reading the worker.** I first concluded "the request never reached the worker, because the worker answers plain-text 401 on bad auth and we got an HTML 403". **Invalid**: the worker passes the upstream response through verbatim (`new Response(data, { status: upstreamRes.status })`), so an origin block page is byte-identical whether proxied or not. The only shape that PROVES the worker was reached is its own 401. Same class as everything else this week — reading a downstream artifact as evidence about an upstream hop.
- **Resolved the guard tension I had filed as "real and unresolved".** `api-admin-discover-moment-descriptors.test.ts` forbids posting All Day to a `TS_PROXY_URL` subpath (a V1 404), which looked like it contradicted CLAUDE.md's "the worker exposes /allday". It does not: per the README **`ALLDAY_PROXY_URL` IS a worker subpath already**, so the guard's rule is about **where the URL comes from** (read the configured variable; never rebuild it and let the two drift), not about what it may point at. **Keep the guard.** Probe comment rewritten from "unresolved operator question" to the actual finding.
- **Also found:** the worker **never 404s on an unknown path** — `UPSTREAM_MAP[path] ? path : DEFAULT_ROUTE` silently proxies a typo'd route to **Top Shot**, so a misrouted All Day query returns a confusing GraphQL field error instead of failing loudly. A `400` would be better; that is a `wrangler deploy` and operator-gated.
- **Filed** `docs/overnight/inbox/2026-08-14T0500Z-allday-waf-403-is-a-one-line-env-fix.md` with the env value, the two-reason justification, the invalid-inference warning, and a verification that needs only a probe re-run. ⚠ It notes an env change requires a REAL rebuild — `vercel.json`'s `ignoreCommand` skips an empty or docs-only commit.
- **Verified:** `tsc` clean; primary **11,716 green**; the 16 probe tests green.
- **Revert:** `git revert <sha>` — comments + a filing only; nothing to unwind in the DB.

### 2026-08-13 · SHIPPED (Claude Code, interactive, cont.) — captured the player bio the probe found: `editions.player_{birthdate,birthplace,draft_year}` (**MIGRATION + ingest**)

Putting them on `players` would have meant touching `upsert_player_canonical`, which is one of the 125 drift-guarded DB pins — materially higher risk for no product gain. **Prefixed `player_`** because `editions` already has `game_date` and `first_minted_at`, so a bare `birthdate` on an EDITION row reads as a date about the moment.
- ⚠ **The placement risk was REAL and is now pinned.** Commit `b1018e63` already shipped this exact class once: `description` was put inside `stats { }`, which invalidates the WHOLE GraphQL query — Top Shot answers **HTTP 422**, `fetchPage` returns null, and the walk **upserts ZERO editions while reporting `ok: true`**. - ⚠ **Sentinel-normalized, which is not optional here.** Top Shot answers `draftYear: 0`, `"N/A"`, `""` rather than null for unknown bio. A raw `?? null` would store `draft_year = 0` for every player with unknown draft data, and the "serial matches draft year" hook would then fire on garbage. All three go through `isSentinel()` — the same guard the description path uses — pinned by a test that reads the ASSIGNMENT line specifically.
- ⚠ **I did NOT capture `jerseyNumber` here even though it is available.** `editions.jersey_number` already exists at **65.3%** coverage, written by a different path; adding a second writer that returns null for un-hydrated rows would clobber good values on every walk — the documented never-null-out trap. - **Arrived at CI-RED `main`** (`79b5b2f6` + `51ba2321`, `Unit tests (vitest)` failing): `api-og-cards-render-sweep` → `Error: Unsupported OpenType signature <!DO`. `<!DO` is the first four bytes of `<!DOCTYPE`.
- ⚠ **ROOT CAUSE, and it is a live product bug rather than a test artifact: `/fonts/*.ttf` was never publicly reachable.** `STATIC_EXT_RX` in `proxy.ts` lists `png|jpe?g|svg|webp|ico|css|js` — **no `ttf`** — and the middleware matcher does not exclude `/fonts/`, so every font request ran the auth gate, failed `isPublicPath`, and was **302'd to `/login`**. Both consumers fetch over HTTP with **no session**: the OG profile card (`runtime = "edge"`, so it *cannot* read the files off disk) and the trophy-case PDF. The followed redirect returns an HTML page at **status 200**, which satisfies `res.ok` and `byteLength > 0` — the only two checks either loader made.
- ⚠ **THE DURABLE PART: the fallback written for exactly this hazard was structurally incapable of firing.** `og/profile` wraps its render in a three-tier try/catch whose comment says a rejected font "THROWS out of ImageResponse rather than degrading" — correct, and guarding the wrong place. **`new ImageResponse(...)` returns a Response whose body is a STREAM**, so satori runs when the body is CONSUMED, after `GET` has already returned; the throw escapes the handler and no `catch` around the constructor will ever see it. **A guard around `new ImageResponse(...)` catches nothing that happens during rendering.**
- ⚠ **And the test that should have caught it modelled the tidy failure instead of the real one.** `api-og-profile-brand-fonts` stubbed the font fetch as a **503** — a shape the old `res.ok` check already handled — so it ran green while production was broken. The new case stubs a **200 whose body is HTML**, reads `arrayBuffer()` (asserting on the returned Response alone passes while the card is broken), and requires the output to equal the no-fonts render so bad bytes cannot be accepted as a typeface. **Mutation-proven: it reproduces `Unsupported OpenType signature <!DO` exactly when the byte check is disabled.**
- **Shipped, two halves.** (1) `lib/og/font-bytes.ts` → `isSupportedFontBuffer` validates the sfnt signature before any renderer sees the bytes — **the response proves the request succeeded, never that a font came back** — wired into both loaders, accepting `ArrayBuffer` or any view since the two callers hold different shapes. WOFF2 is rejected deliberately (opentype.js cannot decode Brotli; accepting it would trade a clear rejection for the same late throw). (2) `proxy.ts` publishes the fonts.
- ⚠ **The `proxy.ts` change is deliberately NARROWER than my first version, which folded `ttf|otf|woff2?` into `STATIC_EXT_RX`.** That regex matches ANY path ending in the extension, so it would also publish a gated route whose trailing dynamic segment a visitor controls. Replaced with a separate **`FONT_ASSET_RX = ^/fonts/[^/]+\.(ttf|otf|woff2?)$`** — directory AND extension, single level. Do not "simplify" it back. Mutation-proven (removing the line reds 5 table rows), and the table pins the negatives: `/fonts`, `/fonts/list`, `/fonts/a/b.ttf`, `/fonts/x.ttf.json`, `/dashboard/report.ttf`, `/api/profile/trophy.woff2` all stay gated.

- **Generalized the finding rather than stopping at the symptom:** swept `public/` for every extension the allowlist misses. It turned up **`/llms.txt`** — the AI-crawler sibling of `robots.txt`, shipped deliberately, **302'ing to `/login`**, i.e. the one file whose entire purpose is to be fetched anonymously was the one file they could not read. Added as an EXACT path (allowlisting `.txt` would publish the OFL license files by side effect rather than by decision). `offline.html` has no referencing code and was left alone.
- ⚠ **Scope note, stated plainly: this modifies the auth wall, which CLAUDE.md lists as off-limits for the autonomous night pass.** Taken here because CI on `main` was red, both changes only publish files already shipped in `public/`, the gate's failure mode (302 → HTML 200) is what makes the outage invisible, and each is pinned by mutation-proven table rows in the primary coverage gate. **Revert:** `git revert <sha>` restores both the wall and the byte check; no DB unwind.

### 2026-08-13 · SHIPPED (Claude Code, interactive, cont.) — a regex in code I shipped 20 minutes earlier would have thrown at PARSE time on older Safari, taking the whole chat down

- **Code + tests, direct to `main`. No DB, no migration, no cron, no auth/`proxy.ts`, no hot-wallet, no FMV/pricing-MATH change.** Follow-up to `7114dc9e`; found by reviewing my own diff after it deployed READY, not by a failure.
- ⚠ **The bug: `SITE_PATH` used a LOOKBEHIND — `(?<=[\s(])` — which is ES2018.** Safari only gained lookbehind in **16.4** (March 2023), and an unsupported regex literal is a **`SyntaxError` at PARSE time**, not a caught runtime error: the module fails to evaluate, `SupportChat` fails to import, and **the entire concierge disappears** for that user. On a product whose own system prompt says "most users are on mobile", that is the worst possible blast radius for a cosmetic linkifier.
- ⚠ **`tsc` cannot save you here and neither can the `target` setting.** `tsconfig.json` says `ES2017`, but TypeScript **does not transpile regex literals** — the pattern ships to the browser byte-for-byte. Every gate was green (tsc clean, 11,395 tests, both coverage ratchets) because **the whole toolchain runs on Node, which has supported lookbehind since v8.3**. There was no signal anywhere in CI; only reading the diff with a browser-support question in mind found it.
- **Fix:** the leading context is now a **capture group** (`(^|[\s(])(\/[a-z]…)`) and the parser offsets by group 1's length. Same behaviour — the "and/or" / "8/13" false-positive guard still holds, all 33 prior tests unchanged and green — with no ES2018 syntax.
- **Guard `source guard — no ES2018-only regex syntax`** asserts the tokenizer contains no `(?<=` / `(?<!`, comments stripped first (the trap hit twice already today). It is a *source* guard because a Node-based test suite is structurally incapable of catching this class: the engine running the tests supports the syntax the target engine does not.
- **Verified:** `tsc` clean; primary gate **11,397 tests green, 91.57 st / 78.91 br**; the three chat suites (27) green. Deploy `dpl_6U2xcHfYvXURaaZWns9uqutCTztJ` (the parent commit) confirmed **READY** and aliased to www before this follow-up.
- **Revert:** `git revert <sha>` — restores the lookbehind, so do not revert this one in isolation.

### 2026-08-13 · SHIPPED (Claude Code, interactive — weekly-QA handoff: entity pages hang on "SCANNING THE MARKETPLACE…") — the entity-page RPC path had NO wall-clock bound, so a call that never ANSWERED parked the render until Vercel killed the function at 300s

**The handoff's own open question — transient or persistent? — was the first thing measured, and it is BOTH.** Re-probed all five entity routes live: every one renders now (edition 3.2s / 11.1s, player 7.8s, team 17.2s, set 16.6s, series 1.1s), so the reported 15-minute window had cleared. But the defect is real and permanent, and production names it: the project's LARGEST runtime-error group is **`Vercel Runtime Timeout Error: Task timed out after 300 seconds` (781 events / 183 users)** and **`/[collection]/edition/[slug]` is one of the routes listed in it**.

⚠ **DURABLE — retrying handles an RPC that FAILS; nothing handled one that never answers, and they are not the same event.** `supabase-js` issues a plain `fetch` with **no signal**, and `rpcWithRetry` had no timeout, so a stuck connection-acquire inside Supavisor parked the `await` indefinitely (undici's own ceiling is ~300s). The retry loop never ran — there was no error to retry. Proven with a positive control: a server that accepts the connection and never responds leaves the call **still hanging at 1.5s**; with `AbortSignal.timeout(800)` it settles in **809ms**, and the abort **RETURNS** an error (does not throw) with **`code: ""`**, so it falls through to the message heuristics. Same lesson the boards learned on 08-12 (`BOARD_LIVE_TIMEOUT_MS`): **slow and broken are equally unservable, and only broken was modelled.**

⚠ **Why it is invisible to every existing instrument.** These five routes ship a `loading.tsx`, so Next flushes the shell and a **200** immediately and streams the page after. A render that never finishes therefore shows the skeleton with **no error, no failing status, and no client XHR** — the API smoke gate sees 200, the DB monitor sees a healthy instance (measured mid-incident: 5 active backends, 0 DataFileRead waiters, RPCs 19–360ms), and the only trace is Vercel's own kill 300s later.

**Shipped** — `lib/analytics/rpc-with-retry.ts` gains a **TOTAL** wall-clock budget (`timeoutMs`, default `DEFAULT_RPC_TIMEOUT_MS = 45_000`) covering all attempts + backoff, not a per-attempt allowance (a per-attempt bound silently multiplies by `attempts`). Two mechanisms on purpose: `.abortSignal()` genuinely cancels and **releases the pool slot** (abandoning a request that still holds a connection makes a pile-up worse), and a `Promise.race` **guarantees** we settle — necessary because every mock in this repo shapes `.rpc` as a bare async fn with no `.abortSignal`, so the signal cannot be relied on to exist.

⚠ **45s is a ceiling ABOVE the database's own, not a latency target — do NOT tune it down.** A statement that is genuinely RUNNING is already bounded (`service_role` `statement_timeout=30s` → 57014, which is deliberately never retried). Anything outstanding past 45s is not a statement, it is a stuck acquire — the one case with no other stop condition. A tighter bound would start cancelling statements Postgres would have finished and answered, and these pages really do render in 11–17s under load. This is **confirmed by the concurrent `2026-08-13T2115Z` inbox finding**, which measures `get_series_detail` at **20,172ms** dying on Postgres's own statement timeout into a retryable error boundary: a 15–20s bound would have pre-empted that handled path with our own abort. The two findings are complementary — that one is the SLOW case (fix = materialize latest FMV), this one is the NO-ANSWER case.

⚠ **A test corrected a design claim I had written.** My first test asserted a timeout is transient so a retry can follow. It is not: each attempt is handed the **remaining** budget, so an attempt that times out has consumed all of it and no retry can follow. That is deliberate — the tempting "fix" (slice the budget per attempt so a retry fits) caps one statement below the 30s `service_role` allows. Test and code comment both corrected to state the real behaviour, and the reasoning is pinned so nobody "fixes" it back.

**Also closed the gap that would have left the fix cosmetic:** the shell's `Promise.all` had **three fetchers on a bare `.rpc()`**, bypassing the wrapper entirely — `get_edition_market_bundle` (the single most frequent edition error in prod: 40 statement timeouts + 17 pool timeouts), `get_edition_insight_links`, and `get_badge_display_metadata` in `lib/badges/server-art.ts`. All three now go through `rpcWithRetry`, which returns the same `{ data, error }` shape they already destructure, so their bespoke `EMPTY_*` fallbacks are unchanged. The other four entity routes were already fully on the bounded path (swept: 0 bare `.rpc(` in each).

**Verified.** `tsc` clean. Both new behaviours **mutation-proven**: removing the bound reds 4 tests (they hang to vitest's 5s cap — the production symptom reproduced in the suite), and firing the guard at 0ms reds the slow-but-OK case, which proves that case is **not vacuous** (the documented microtask-beats-the-timer trap). New tests stress-run **10/10 stable**. Full primary coverage gate: **3 files / 7 tests failing, byte-identical to the clean-tree baseline** measured by stashing the change and re-running (the documented local-env `INGEST_SECRET_TOKEN` reds, green in CI) — **0 threshold errors**. ⚠ Method note: `npm run test:coverage ... | tail` reports **`tail`'s** exit code, not vitest's — it printed a green exit over a red run and briefly hid the 8th failure; that 8th was then shown to be a flake, not my change, only by the stash-and-compare.

**Known remaining (NOT fixed, deliberately scoped):** two `.from()` TABLE reads on the edition page (`fetchPackProvenance`, `fetchOwnerUsernames`) are still unbounded. They sit BELOW the `<Suspense>` boundary, so they cannot cause the reported shell hang — they would strand a lower section, not the skeleton — and bounding PostgREST table builders needs a different helper than this RPC-shaped one.

**Revert:** `git revert <sha>` (code-only; no DB, migration, cron, auth/`proxy.ts`, hot-wallet or FMV/pricing-MATH change).

### 2026-08-13 · SHIPPED (Claude Code, interactive) — the Panini backup grew past Node's max string length, so the recovery tool it exists to feed could no longer read it

**Shipped** (Cowork cloud authored the patch; both its push routes were closed, so it handed off a verified diff — applied, re-verified against the REAL file, and pushed here).

`scripts/ingest-panini-runner.mjs` — `PANINI_BACKUP_FILE` (`panini-capture.jsonl`) was appended before every POST, on every batch, of every 4-hourly walk, with **no cap, no rotation, no prune-on-success**. Measured on Trevor's box: **1,268,982,254 B (1.21 GiB)**, ~26 days live ⇒ ~46 MB/day. Added `appendBackup()` with `PANINI_BACKUP_MAX_BYTES` (default 100 MB) + rotate-to-`.1`. ⚠ **The bound it needed already existed 87 lines below it** — the *optional* ops-capture is correctly capped at 25 MB with one generation (19.8 MB + 26.2 MB on disk, working as designed). The always-on disaster-recovery file, written far more often, got no such treatment.

`scripts/panini-replay.mjs` — rewritten to stream via `readline` over `createReadStream`, and to replay the **rotated generation first** (`.1`, then live) in capture order.

**⚠ DURABLE — the disk was the small half. `readFileSync(FILE,"utf8")` materializes the whole file as ONE JavaScript string, and Node caps a single string at `MAX_STRING_LENGTH` = 536,870,888 B on 64-bit. At 2.36× that, the recovery tool the backup EXISTS to feed threw before POSTing a single batch — a safety net that fails only at the exact moment it is needed** (bad token, walk to recover), and fails silently until then. Verified here against the **actual 1.21 GiB file**, not a fixture: old path `ERR_STRING_TOO_LONG`; new path streamed **15,279 batches in 3.7 s, 0 parse failures**.

**Verification:** `node --check` both. Rotation tested against the **verbatim shipped bytes** (extracted with `sed` from the patched file) across caps 30/100/1000 B, one fresh process per cap — pinned: total never exceeds 2× cap, newest batch always retained, fresh file never rotates. Replay tested end-to-end against a local server: ordering `old-1, old-2, new-1, new-2`, blanks skipped, CRLF handled. ⚠ My first rotation harness failed at cap=30 and **the harness was wrong, not the code** — `BACKUP_MAX_BYTES` is a module-load-time `const`, so mutating `process.env` inside a loop never took effect; re-run with a fresh process per cap, all three pass. (Cowork recorded the same class of error on its own first assertion.)

**Scope:** local-only runner scripts on the residential box. No route, DB, migration, cron, auth/`proxy.ts`, hot-wallet or FMV/pricing change. `panini-capture.jsonl` is gitignored (`.gitignore:125`, `panini*capture*.jsonl*`), so `git add -A` was never at risk.

**Space reclaimed (done, same session): 1,210 MiB.** ⚠ **The fix validated itself in production before I could act on it, and that is the transferable part.** The runner reads `scripts/` straight from the working tree, so its next 4-hourly walk picked up the patched code and the cap **fired on the real 1.21 GiB file**, rotating it to `.1` — confirmation on the actual artifact, not a fixture. It also moved the target between my measurement and the confirmation, and I truncated the **live** file (4.8 MB, mid-walk) before noticing. No loss — the backup is written BEFORE the POST and those POSTs were landing (78 rows in the following 10 min, newest 0.3 min old) — but that was luck, not design: **re-stat a destructive target after any pause, because a live writer can rename it out from under a plan that was correct when it was made.** The 1.21 GiB `.1` was then truncated on the evidence that every batch in it was already ingested (its 17:23 mtime matched the newest `panini_fmv_snapshots` row exactly). ⚠ **Cowork's stated reason for it being safe to delete — "already unrecoverable by the tool that consumes it" — was disproven by this very ship**: streaming replay reads it fine (15,279 batches). Same verdict, different reason; the honest one is "already ingested", not "unreadable". **Unrelated to the `/sessions` no-space shell outage** (Cowork VM disk, not the Windows host) — that is still "delete old Cowork sessions", ~6 nights.

**Revert:** `git revert <sha>` — restores the unbounded append and the slurping replay. No DB unwind. To keep the code but disable the bound, set `PANINI_BACKUP_MAX_BYTES` very high.

### 2026-08-13 · SHIPPED (Claude Code, interactive — session close) — consolidated the session's durable lessons into the CANONICAL sections, because dated entries roll off in ~3 days

- **Docs-only push to `main`** (CLAUDE.md). **No code, DB, migration or prod-state change.**
- **Why this entry exists at all.** Ledger and Recent-sessions entries are frozen history and roll off to `docs/sessions/` within ~3 days. **A lesson left only in a dated entry stops being found by the sections a future session actually reads** — which is precisely how five canonical figures drifted earlier this month. So the session's transferable findings were moved into the canonical bullets, not just recorded.
- **The most load-bearing addition: a rule on `apply_migration` itself.** Every migration causes a **~10-20 s burst of user-facing 500s** (PostgREST schema-cache re-introspection → `PGRST002`). Measured causally, not inferred: all schema-cache events in 24 h fell in one 11-second span, first error **+10 s** after the migration, last **+21 s**. It carries the mitigation (**prefer a low-traffic window; batching N migrations into one window costs one burst instead of N**), the ⚠ that `rpcWithRetry`'s ~250 ms of backoff does **not** cover it, and the ⚠ against "fixing" it by making the pages fail soft (the throw is deliberate, deep-audit D10).

- **The cause, measured.** Every schema-cache event in the trailing 24 h falls inside **one 11-second window** — 17:20:15 / :21 / :23 / :26 Z, across the pack, edition and player pages. `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations` shows `audit_20260813_pack_rips_collection_block_height_index` applied at **17:20:05 Z**. **The first 500 lands 10 s after the migration, the last 21 s after it.** Applying a migration invalidates PostgREST's schema cache; every request served during the re-introspection gets `PGRST002`, which our pages surface as a 500.
- **So these errors are not saturation, not upstream, and not random — we cause them, every time we ship a migration.** That is the entire explanation for 81 users / 84 events accruing since 2026-07-18: a handful of real visitors caught per reload window, across many migrations. Three migrations landed within 11 minutes today.
- ⚠ **Why the retry is necessary but NOT sufficient, arithmetically:** `rpcWithRetry` is 3 attempts at 50 ms + 200 ms ≈ **250 ms of retrying**, against a **~10-20 second** reload window. All three attempts land inside the first quarter-second of a twenty-second outage. **Do not treat `NEXTJS-1Z` as closed by `4f303102`** — expect it on the next migration.
- **In-code comment corrected in the same push.** It previously said "if telemetry shows retries still failing, the next lever is a longer backoff — not taken on speculation." The telemetry now exists, so the comment states the measured window and explicitly says the clause must not be read as "NEXTJS-1Z is solved".
- **Options filed with the trade-off stated, none taken:** (1) lengthen the backoff for this class only (~17 s of coverage fits the 45 s budget) — ⚠ but that converts a 500 into a **~20 s render holding a lambda and pool slot**, with many concurrent requests holding at once; a product/cost call, not an obvious win. (2) Apply migrations in a low-traffic window — cheapest, no code. (3) Accept it, and stop re-investigating it as a mystery.
- ⚠ **Do NOT "fix" it by making the pages fail soft** — the throw is deliberate on all three (deep-audit D10) so a transient failure renders a retryable error boundary rather than a soft-404 that invites Google to drop a real page. That would trade a visible 20 s blip for silent SEO damage.
- **Method note worth keeping:** found by correlating two clocks nobody had put side by side — Sentry event timestamps and `schema_migrations.version` (which encodes applied time as `YYYYMMDDHH24MISS`). **When an error looks like random infrastructure noise, check whether it tracks our own migrations or deploys before blaming the platform.**

- ⚠ **An EMPTY-but-successful catalog read is deliberately NOT treated as inconclusive**, and that distinction is tested. If the catalog genuinely holds no priced row for the characters under test, a priced deal row really IS unbacked — which is the leak this guard exists to catch. **Only a FAILED read is inconclusive.** Blanket-skipping on empty would have disarmed the guard while appearing to fix it.
- **Mutation-proven, and the mutation reproduces the production incident verbatim:** flipping the new `if (catalogErr)` to a constant-false makes the test emit `FMV leaked on 2 row(s): Goofy/Disney Holiday Vol.1/Colored Enamel fmv=$0.77` — a leak report manufactured entirely from a pool timeout. ⚠ My first mutation attempt spliced the file by string index, broke it syntactically and reported `no tests`; **a mutation that stops the suite parsing proves nothing** — redone as a clean one-token change.

### 2026-08-13 · SHIPPED (Claude Code, interactive, cont.) — the platform's single largest user-facing error was a retryable failure we never retried once (81 users, a month old)

- **Code + tests to `main`**: `lib/analytics/rpc-with-retry.ts` + 4 tests. **No DB, migration, cron, auth, hot-wallet or FMV-math change.** Fixes Sentry `JAVASCRIPT-NEXTJS-1Z`.
- ⚠ **Found only because I widened the Sentry query.** The earlier sweep this session filtered `firstSeen:-3d` and surfaced one small issue. Dropping that filter changed the picture completely: the dominant error is **not** a statement timeout but PostgREST's **`Could not query the database for the schema cache. Retrying.`** — `NEXTJS-1Z` (pack dist) **81 users / 84 events, first seen 2026-07-18**, plus `NEXTJS-26` (edition, 40 events) and `NEXTJS-20` (player, 12) — ~97 events in 7 days, still firing. Real traffic: a Chrome/Windows user in Singapore on `/nfl-all-day/pack/dist/6510`. **A "new issues only" filter hid the biggest one for being a month old.**
- **The defect: all three paths ALREADY went through `rpcWithRetry`** (`lib/pack-dist/fetchers.ts:246`, `lib/entity-detail-gate.ts:61`) — but `isTransient` matched none of the heuristics against this message (no "timeout", "timed out", "network", "connection pool"), and the code is `PGRST002`, not a SQLSTATE, so the code tests missed it too. **A failure PostgREST itself labels "Retrying." was never retried once, for a month.**
- ⚠ **The careful part — PostgREST has TWO lookalike "schema cache" messages meaning opposite things, and the naive fix gets it wrong.** `PGRST002` "**Could not query** the database for the schema cache" = introspection failed to reach the DB (saturation / just after DDL) → **transient, RETRY**. `PGRST205` "Could not find the table/function … **in the schema cache**" = the cache loaded fine and the object genuinely is not there, a deploy or naming bug → **NEVER retry**; retrying only burns the budget to fail identically. The exclusion is tested FIRST so the broader match cannot swallow it.
- **Mutation-proven in BOTH directions, and the second is the one that matters:** removing the PGRST002 clause reds 2 tests; replacing the precise match with a bare `"schema cache"` substring (the obvious implementation) reds the PGRST205 tests — i.e. the naive version is demonstrably wrong, not just less precise.
- **Safety checked before widening:** `rpcWithRetry` is 3 attempts with 50/200 ms backoff inside the shared 45 s budget, so this adds a bounded amount of work and cannot loop. Noted in-code that if telemetry shows retries still failing, the next lever is a longer backoff for this class specifically — not taken on speculation.
- **Verified:** `tsc` clean; full suite **1165 files / 11311 tests**; primary gate 91.55 st / 78.91 br / 93.41 fn / 93.67 ln (thresholds 90.4/77.0/92.2/92.6).

### 2026-08-13 · SHIPPED (Claude Code, interactive, cont.) — bounded the edition page's last two unbounded reads, the remainder a concurrent session deliberately scoped out

- **Code + tests to `main`**: new `lib/edition/fetchers.ts`, `withQueryDeadline` in `lib/analytics/rpc-with-retry.ts`, the edition page rewired, 9 new tests. **No DB, migration, cron, auth, hot-wallet or FMV-math change.**

Both are live production error sources — `[edition] pack provenance Timed out acquiring connection from connection pool.` (**19 events**) and `[edition] owner_usernames …` (**5 events**).
- ⚠ **The filing suggested writing a second primitive; it did not need one, and I said so rather than following the spec.** `withDeadline` (already in that module) only ever probes for `.abortSignal` — nothing in it is RPC-specific — so it already accepts any thenable builder. `withQueryDeadline` is a **thin exported wrapper over it**. One mechanism with one set of edge cases beats two that can drift.
- **Deliberately NO retry**, unlike `rpcWithRetry`: these are supplementary sections, and a retry doubles the worst-case hold on the pool that is itself the thing saturating. The deadline releases the slot, which is the half that matters. **Kept the 45 s default** — a tighter client bound would pre-empt Postgres's own `statement_timeout=30s`, the handled path that turns a slow query into a retryable error boundary (see the companion `2115Z` file, where `get_series_detail` legitimately runs ~20 s).
- ⚠ **Both fetchers fail SOFT and that is correct HERE — recorded so nobody "fixes" it into a throw.** Neither failure renders a false claim: provenance renders only when `pack_pulls_observed > 0`, so a failed read HIDES a supplementary section rather than claiming "0 pulls"; usernames fall back to the raw address, which is still true. They are **omissions, not assertions**. `{ data, ok }` is returned anyway so the distinction exists the moment either moves above the fold.
- ⚠ **CORRECTION to the filing, and it is why the ratchet did NOT move.** It said extracting these two "would satisfy the ratchet's stated remedy". It does not: `server-page-data-access-ratchet` keys on the **`@/lib/supabase` import**, and the page still imports it for two `rpcWithRetry` call sites. **BUDGET stays 36.** Extracting those two as well is a separate, larger refactor — their types (`MarketBundle`/`HighOffer`/`IpfsAsset`/`SubeditionSibling`) are page-local and used in rendering — and they are already bounded, i.e. no defect. Not worth doing inside a file another session is actively editing.
- **9 tests, mutation-proven.** Replacing `withQueryDeadline` with a bare await makes the two "never comes back" cases **hang to the runner's timeout** — which is precisely the production behaviour (render parked until Vercel's 300 s kill, section spinning forever). Also pinned: `ok:false` vs empty-with-`ok:true`, the All Day vs Top Shot view selection (reading the wrong view is a silent correctness bug, not a visible failure), that an empty address list issues **no query at all**, and that an `AbortSignal` is passed when the builder supports one — because racing settles US, only the abort releases the CONNECTION.
- **Verified:** `tsc` clean; full suite **1161 files / 11201 tests**; primary gate 91.50 st / 78.64 br / 93.31 fn / 93.65 ln (thresholds 90.4/77.0/92.2/92.6); ratchet + `server-pages-error-vs-absent-guard` + `analytics-rpc-with-retry` all green.
- **Revert:** `git revert <sha>` — restores the inline unbounded fetchers. Nothing to unwind in prod or the DB.

No index, no DB change. It also closes a real hole: a lone history backfill ticking away used to SATISFY the check while every forward indexer was dead.
- **The expensive scan is kept for the one case that needs it.** When the bounded probe reads exactly zero — an incident is already indicated — the unbounded count runs to separate **"forward ingest is dead" from "everything is dead"**, a distinction the old check could not make at all. So the common path is ~half the cost and the failure path is strictly more informative.
- **Verified against live data before arming it:** the stricter predicate returns **539 rows** in the last 2h right now, a healthy margin over the `crit_at` floor of 0 — so this does not arm a false page. A count merely *below a configured floor* is reported as a threshold breach and explicitly **does not** say "ZERO" (that would be a false statement about the data) and does not pay for the second scan.
- **5 new tests, mutation-proven.** The load-bearing one **records the FILTERS** the route applies, because the shared fixture's chainables discard their arguments — a test asserting only the resulting status would pass just as happily with the `sold_at` bound deleted, i.e. would assert nothing about the change. Deleting the bound reds it with "sold_at bound missing — the planner would scan all 8 partitions". Also pinned: the healthy path issues **exactly one** query, the below-floor path issues one, and the zero path issues two.
- **Both misleading notes corrected in place** — CLAUDE.md's "superseded" sentence and the route header's "drop the seq-scan" prescription — since either would have led the next session to delete a live tripwire.
- **Verified:** `tsc` clean; full suite **1153 files / 11005 tests**; primary gate 91.18 st / 78.01 br / 92.88 fn / 93.34 ln (thresholds 90.4/77.0/92.2/92.6). Component gate untouched (no `components/**` change).

- **Code + tests to `main`.** 67 route files + `lib/api-error.ts` + 2 new test files; no DB, migration, cron, auth/`proxy.ts`, hot-wallet, or FMV/pricing-MATH change.

But that same design **fixes its scope**: everything behind sign-in was outside it *by construction*. Measured: **158 sites / 97 files** outside `/api/admin` + `/api/cron`, of which **120 across 64 files were user-facing** (the rest are operator-secret-gated, the same rationale that excuses admin/cron).
- ⚠ **One was rendered STRAIGHT INTO A TOAST.** `app/dashboard/page.tsx` throws `data.error` from `/api/profile/trophy/reorder` and shows it — so a statement timeout was displayed to a collector as the reason their trophy case did not save. That route also **branches on the message** to pick 409-vs-500; reading it server-side to classify is fine, publishing it was not, so the 409 now carries its own actionable copy.
- **Applied by a codemod on exact `(file, line)` matches, never a broad regex** — this repo has a documented incident where one hit 351 files instead of 18. It **deferred 13 sites** whose body carried contract keys (`ok:false`, `matched:true`, `code`, `stats`, `rows`, `results`) and those were done by hand. `matched: true` was preserved deliberately: "your listing DID match and only the recording failed" is a different thing to tell a user than "no match".

(2) Its ternary pattern was too permissive and silently dropped `rows: []` / `results: []` from two bodies. That drop turned out to be *correct* (empty data beside a 500 lets a caller who skips `res.ok` render "no market data" from an internal error, same call as `pack-pulls`) — but it is now **deliberate and commented**, not accidental.
- ⚠ **`safeApiError` only knows Postgres, so blanket-applying it DESTROYS an actionable caller error.** Four routes throw their own `"Could not resolve …"` for a bad username; classifying that as `internal` replaced the one thing the user needed to be told with "Something went wrong." and returned **500 for what is a 400**. New `isUnresolvedIdentifierError()` / `unresolvedIdentifierResponse()` in `lib/api-error.ts` — classify on the message server-side, publish **fixed copy**, 400 + `code: "not_found"`.
- **59 existing tests asserted the leak**, two titled *"500s and **surfaces the message**"* — a title that makes the defect read as the contract. Rewritten to `not.toContain(<driver text>)` and retitled.
- **The durable half: `__tests__/helpers/driver-message-leak.ts` is now the ONE source of the five spellings**, imported by both guards. This directly answers the recorded failure where the anon guard shipped with four spellings against its predecessor's five and 12 sites kept leaking — a new spelling now widens both guards at once. New `authed-api-no-driver-message-leak-guard` covers the signed-in surface, **asserts its own operator-exclusions really carry a secret gate**, and asserts the anon guard's set is a **subset** of its own so no route falls between them. Mutation-proven (re-introducing the leak in `/api/portfolio` reds it).

### 2026-08-12 · SHIPPED — DB ×2 + code half in a patch (Cowork cloud) · both wmc FMV propagation writers had been dead on EVERY tick for 10+ hours, invisibly; drift sweep made resumable, failures made visible

**The outage.** `refresh_wmc_fmv_changed` AND `refresh_wmc_fmv_drift_active` were both failing
`57014 canceling statement due to statement timeout` on **every 5-minute tick** — confirmed in Vercel
runtime logs, 9 of 9 sampled ticks, both RPCs — while `pipeline_runs` showed **988 runs / 0 failures
in 12h**. They log only to `console.log`; the per-collection rows come from `runOne` (which
succeeds) and the route returns 202 by design, so **nothing DB-side could alert.**
`rwfd_state.last_cutoff` was frozen at 12:53:59Z, **10h27m stale**.

**Root cause (measured, not inferred).** `service_role` carries `statement_timeout=30s`
(`pg_roles.rolconfig`), and the route calls both RPCs through supabase-js → PostgREST → service_role.
`refresh_wmc_fmv_drift_active` declared `SET statement_timeout TO '120s'` — **inert**, per the proven
`proconfig`-cannot-raise-the-calling-statement's-budget finding — and `refresh_wmc_fmv_changed`
sets a 60s internal deadline, **twice the budget it actually has**, so it can never fire before the
kill. Run by hand with a **55s** budget the drift sweep still timed out, so this was never a
"widen the timeout" problem.

⚠ **Not lock contention — I checked and it isn't.** `pg_blocking_pids()` was empty for every
backend; the instance is **I/O-starved** (11+ authenticator backends parked 15–30s in
`DataFileRead`/`BufferIo`, a `cron_heavy backfill_nft_edition_map_from_sales` at 122s in
`DataFileRead`). Job 302's runs also do **not** overlap the route's ticks (measured: 0 of 12).

**Shipped (2 migrations, signature unchanged so no new overload, grants verified intact — SECDEF,
`service_role`+`postgres` EXECUTE only, `check_secdef_anon_execute_violations()` = `[]`):**

- `audit_20260812_drift_active_chunked_resumable` — chunked loop, deadline **inside** the 30s
  budget, `p_limit` now **honoured** (it was accepted and never referenced — a budget knob that did
  nothing), the misleading inert `SET statement_timeout` removed, and **the ratchet eliminated**:
  `last_cutoff` now advances to just below the oldest UNPROCESSED edition, so a partial run banks
  its progress instead of widening the next attempt.
- `audit_20260812_drift_active_chunk_sized_for_saturation` — chunk 100→**25**, deadline 20s→**15s**,
  sized to FIT the current I/O budget rather than to finish.

**✅ Verified working:** `last_cutoff` advanced **12:53:59Z → 13:08:58Z** — the first forward
progress in 10.5 hours. ⚠ **Converging, not fixed:** ~1 chunk/tick under present saturation, so the
8,027-edition backlog drains slowly. Watch `rwfd_state.last_cutoff` — if it stops advancing again,
the next lever is chunking by wmc ROWS rather than by editions.

**Code half — NOT pushed from the cloud session; patch `0003-wmc-propagation-pipeline-runs-logging.patch`.**
`runRefresh()` records each RPC in `pipeline_runs` under its own pipeline name with `p_ok`,
`p_error`, `duration_ms` (`p_collection_slug` null — both are global; a slug would corrupt the

### 2026-08-13 · SHIPPED — CODE ONLY, DEPLOY DELIBERATELY WITHHELD (Claude Code, interactive) — `compute-pinnacle-pack-ev` duplicate-conflict-key upsert

- **The defect.** `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` may not touch one target row twice, so a single duplicated `dist_id` in the batch aborts the WHOLE statement with `21000 ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE command cannot affect row a second time` and discards every other row in the chunk. The throw also skips Phase 3b, so **no `pack_ev_history` row was written either**. Live: 100% failing, identical error on every tick since the last successful write at **2026-08-11 06:17Z**; `pack_distributions` for Pinnacle is 143 rows all stamped that instant. Bounded to Pinnacle pack-EV staleness — no corruption, and unlike the catalog-walker bug this one **logged its error honestly**, which is why it was caught in 2 days rather than by accident.
- **The fix.** New `supabase/functions/_shared/upsert-dedupe.ts` → `dedupeByConflictKey(rows, key)`, wired into Phase 3a. **Last occurrence wins**, so the batched form matches what a sequential per-row upsert would have left. `collection_id` is constant for this function, so `dist_id` alone is the key — the helper's contract requires the key fn use the same columns as the `onConflict` string.
- **⚠ The dedupe is COUNTED, not silent.** `dist_dupe_count` + a 5-key `dist_dupe_sample` now ride both `pipeline_runs.extra` payloads. Quietly collapsing the rows would trade a loud deterministic failure for an invisible one — the exact class fixed on the Top Shot catalog walker the same day. **If `dist_dupe_count` stays non-zero, the studio-platform walk is emitting two nodes under one `dist_id` and THAT is the thing to investigate; this fix stops the crash, it does not explain the duplicate.**
- **Scope checked, not assumed:** the three sibling pack-EV functions (`compute-allday`/`golazos`/`topshot-pack-ev`) carry **no** `onConflict` upsert, so this shape is unique to Pinnacle. `evRows` is deliberately NOT deduped — `pack_ev_history` is append-only history and two listing uuids under one dist is a real upstream state, not a conflict.
- **⚠ NOT DEPLOYED, and the reason is a hard coupling — do not deploy this file alone.** `compute-pinnacle-pack-ev` is **jobid 42, one of D2b's five un-rotated functions**: the repo copy reads `PINNACLE_PACK_EV_GATE_KEY`, that secret is **not set**, and the gate fails CLOSED. Deploying now would turn a deterministic SQL failure into a **403 on every tick** — strictly worse. The deploy must ride the rotation window (set the secret → deploy → repoint the pg_cron `?key=`), or at minimum the operator sets `PINNACLE_PACK_EV_GATE_KEY` to the currently-deployed literal first. Until then Pinnacle pack EV stays frozen at 08-11 06:17Z and the alert stays honestly red.
- **Tests.** `__tests__/edge-upsert-dedupe.test.ts` (8 cases) pins upsert-safety, last-wins, the collision count, the sample cap, first-seen key order, and that `7` and `"7"` collapse to one key (the fn builds `dist_id` with `String(node.id)`, so type-split keys would still be one target row in Postgres). Required anyway by the `edge-shared-test-completeness` rot-guard, which reds CI on any untested `_shared` module.
- **Verified.** `tsc --noEmit` clean; dedupe + rot-guard tests 12/12. ⚠ `deno check` NOT run locally (deno is not installed on this box and `jsr.io` is proxy-blocked) — the blocking `edge-deno` CI job is the check. The new module has zero imports, so the risk is confined to the one added import line.
- **Revert:** `git revert <sha>` — removes the dedupe + counters and deletes the `_shared` module and its test. No DB, cron or deploy change to unwind (nothing was deployed).

### 2026-08-13 · reconcile-saved-wallet-stats soft deadline 100s → 50s (fixes intermittent 120s hard-abort)

`rpc-reconcile-saved-wallet-stats` (pg_cron jobid 259, runs as `postgres`) was flapping to cron
status `failed` on saturated days (2026-08-09 and 2026-08-12, both **exactly 120.0s** = the global
`statement_timeout`; postgres has no role-level override, and `cron_heavy`'s 600s is unreachable
because the proc is invoker-rights, directly writes RLS-protected `saved_wallets`, and `cron_heavy`
is not BYPASSRLS). Root cause: per-wallet `aggregate_saved_wallet_stats` costs **16–55s** under IO
saturation (EXPLAIN: the top-tier correlated subquery does a Bitmap Heap Scan + Sort per collection,
~70% of the plan; the 43k-moment whale wallet `0xf77bf547fccf6656` is the worst case), while the
soft deadline (100s) is only checked BETWEEN wallets — so a single expensive wallet entered near the
100s mark pushed cumulative time past the 120s hard cap and aborted the whole CALL.

Fix: lowered `p_max_seconds` default **100 → 50** in `reconcile_all_saved_wallet_stats` — leaves ~70s
of headroom below the 120s cap for the in-flight wallet, converting the straddle-abort into a clean
`succeeded` truncation (partial progress already commits per-wallet; stalest-first resumes next run).
Body byte-identical otherwise: invoker-rights (COMMIT requires it), no SET clause, same signature →
grants preserved (`postgres` + `service_role` only, verified; not anon/authenticated). Structural
fixes were re-checked and remain correctly declined: array_agg fold (−21%, loses index-only outer
scan — `tier` not in `idx_wmc_cohort_cover`), tier covering index (HOT write amplification on 2.2M-row
wmc), cron_heavy (RLS/BYPASSRLS), schedule move (13:33Z not structurally congested).

Migration: `supabase/migrations/20260813150925_audit_20260813_reconcile_saved_wallet_stats_lower_soft_deadline.sql`
(applied to prod as version `20260813150925`; committed file matches by name — commit it to close the
`migration-parity` window).

Residual (NOT fixed, monitored): a single wallet whose aggregate alone exceeds ~70s under extreme
saturation could still abort — unavoidable without the declined structural work; Check 7 (daily
onboarding watch) surfaces a recurrence. Behavioral proof is the next scheduled run (06:33 PT
2026-08-14) reading `succeeded`; the deployment (new default, invoker, no-SET, grants) is verified.

**Revert (NOT `git revert` — the migration file is not yet committed):**
```

  IN p_max_seconds integer DEFAULT 100, IN p_max_wallets integer DEFAULT 500, IN p_min_age_minutes integer DEFAULT 360)
```

### 2026-08-13 · SHIPPED — **the PRIMITIVE, not a third instance** (Claude Code, interactive, cont. 23) · `summarizeDegraded` silently dropped any status that said "I succeeded, and I know I was cut short"

- **Why this rather than another caller fix.** I fixed the same bug twice today at the call site — panini's status (`7f48e928`) and candy's sections — without touching what LET it happen. The repo's own rule is *"extend the guard, not just the instance"*, and I had not. This closes it at the primitive so there is no third instance to find.
- **The defect:** `summarizeDegraded` opened with `if (s.ok) continue`, so `{ ok: true, partial: true }` was discarded entirely. And `BoardStatus.partial`'s own doc said it was *"meaningless when `ok` is true"* — **the comment licensed the bug.** But that combination is exactly what a read which FILLED A HARD CAP produces: the query succeeded, and the caller knows the answer is incomplete. Dropping it shipped a blank Panini board with no notice earlier today: the fetcher correctly emptied its truncated rows and the sentence explaining the blank never rendered.
- **Fix:** `partial` is now checked FIRST and independently of `ok`, and the type's doc says so. **A caller that knows its read was truncated can no longer be ignored.** The two fetchers still fold truncation into `ok` themselves — belt and braces, deliberately: the call sites read more clearly, and the primitive is now safe regardless.
- **Verified it is a NO-OP for every existing caller before changing it.** All ~20 other board pages build statuses via `boardStatus(label, ok)`, which never sets `partial`; only panini and candy set it, and both already fold. So the change alters behaviour for exactly the shape that was previously a silent bug, and nothing else. `total`-driven pluralisation and the failed/truncated split are untouched.
- **Verified.** 3 new tests, both mutations red (restore the `ok`-first ordering → reds; treat every status as truncated → 5 red). `tsc` clean; primary gate **1150 files, exit 0**; component gate 185 / 1560. CLAUDE.md's board-status bullet now records the `ok` = USABLE rule, that `partial` is honoured regardless of `ok`, that a filled `.limit()` is a truncated ranking, and that **candy's caps are not all the 600 default** (serials 607/**800**, holders 395/**800**).
- **Code + tests + docs only — no DB, cron, auth, or prod-state change. Revert:** `git revert <sha>` (restores the silent drop).

(a) This session resumed across a day boundary and I carried the previous turn's date forward instead of re-reading the clock — the commits are stamped **2026-08-13 07:30 and 07:48 PDT**. A concurrent session hit the identical class and amended the file's own dating rule; the durable form of it is to READ the zone, never assume it (`date '+%Z'` — this sandbox is **PDT**, not UTC, so the reflexive "subtract 7h from `date -u`" lands a day early). (b) **`cont. N` is NOT session-unique** — two sessions increment the same counter, and 08-12 alone carries duplicate 16/19/20/21. A cross-reference by `cont.
